    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A deadly form of blood cancer may begin taking shape more than 50 years before a person is diagnosed, according to newly introduced research revealing the surprisingly long and predictable path to leukemia.

    Scientists have reconstructed how acute myeloid leukemia (AML) develops over a lifetime, discovering that in two-thirds of the cases studied, the first genetic mutation that helped drive the cancer appeared before age 20. These early changes could remain largely unnoticed for decades before eventually contributing to the disease.

    The findings suggest that doctors may one day be able to identify people at risk of developing leukemia years or even decades before symptoms appear. They also raise the possibility of preventing the cancer by slowing the growth of abnormal blood cells long before the disease takes hold.

    Blood Samples Reveal Leukemia's Hidden History.

    Recent findings suggest that published in Nature, the study was conducted by researchers at the University of Cambridge and University College London (UCL). By examining blood samples collected over many years, including some obtained as long as 15 years before diagnosis, the team pieced together a detailed history of how leukemia develops.

    In a recent development, the scientists treated these stored samples as a kind of genetic fossil record. Using highly sensitive DNA sequencing and mathematical models, they worked backward to estimate when cancer-related mutations first appeared, how rapidly the affected cells multiplied, and how they competed with other blood cells as the disease approached.

    AML is an aggressive blood cancer that affects approximately 2,700 people in the UK annually. Its outlook is often poor, with only about one in six patients surviving at least five years after diagnosis.

    According to recent reports, scientists have long known that many otherwise healthy older adults carry blood cells with mutations associated with leukemia. This condition, called clonal hematopoiesis, does not necessarily lead to cancer. In fact, most people with these mutations never develop AML. Until now, researchers have struggled to understand why some individuals progress to leukemia while others do not, partly because they lacked a detailed record of the genetic changes occurring in the years before diagnosis.

    Sources indicate that to investigate, the team turned to samples from the UK Collaborative Trial of Ovarian Cancer Screening (UKCTOCS). That project involved approximately 50,000 women who provided blood samples annually for as long as 11 years.

    For the upcoming analysis, researchers examined samples from 47 women who eventually developed AML, with an average age at diagnosis of 72. They compared these findings with samples from 46 similar women who remained free of blood cancer.

    Cancer Mutations Can Remain Hidden for Decades.

    The results revealed an extraordinary timeline. In two-thirds of the women who developed AML, the earliest mutation contributing to the disease was estimated to have occurred before their 20th birthday.

    It has been revealed that at first, the altered blood cells multiplied extremely slowly, sometimes taking several years just to double in number. But as additional cancer-driving mutations accumulated, their growth accelerated dramatically.

    It has been revealed that each latest mutation typically increased the rate of growth by roughly two to three times. By the time cells had acquired four mutations capable of driving cancer, their populations could double within weeks instead of years.

    Perhaps even more surprising was how consistently these populations behaved.

    Researchers found that groups of genetically related blood cells, known as clones, generally expanded at predictable rates once they became established. Their growth tended to slow only when they faced limited space or competition from another clone that was multiplying more promptly.

    Recent findings suggest that this consistency could have important medical implications. By measuring the growth of a particular clone using just a few blood samples, scientists may be able to estimate how large that population will become many years into the future, potentially even decades later.

    A Hidden Warning Sign of Leukemia.

    The researchers also identified a striking pattern that appeared in some patients well before leukemia was diagnosed.

    In at least one-third of AML cases, a single population of mutated blood cells had grown so extensively that it dominated the blood years before diagnosis. Scientists call this process a "somatic sweep.".

    None of the women in the comparison group who remained free of blood cancer highlighted the same pattern.

    The researchers then examined data from the UK Biobank and confirmed that people showing evidence of these sweeps faced a substantially greater risk of developing AML.

    This finding suggests that somatic sweeps could serve as an vital early warning sign. However, conventional genetic testing can miss them because the mutations involved are sometimes incorrectly classified as inherited genetic variations.

    Professor Jamie Blundell, who led the research at the University of Cambridge's Early Cancer Institute, explained how the team reconstructed the disease's history.

    According to recent reports, "Serial blood samples are a fossil record of the blood's evolution. They let us go back in time and reconstruct when each mutation arose and how fast it grew. What surprised us most is how predictable the growth of these clones is. Once a clone is established, its growth rate today tells you where it will be years, even decades, from now.".

    He added: "Because the growth is exponential, even modestly slowing a high-risk clone over the decade or more before diagnosis could substantially reduce the chance it becomes leukemia. This opens up strategies we can exploit to prevent these clones ever becoming leukemia.".

    Could Leukemia Be Prevented Before It Develops?

    The discovery could change how doctors approach a disease that often appears to develop with little warning.

    Dr. Caroline Watson, the study's first author and a researcher at the Early Cancer Institute, emphasized the contrast between the sudden impact of a leukemia diagnosis and the decades of biological changes that may precede it.

    "As a hematologist, I've seen how suddenly AML can change someone's life. This study demonstrates that the changes leading to AML can build over decades, with the affected cells growing in surprisingly predictable ways.".

    Recent findings suggest that watson is also an Honorary Consultant Haematologist who treats patients at the Cambridge Clonal Haematopoiesis Clinic at Addenbrooke's Hospital. The clinic is the first in Europe dedicated to leukemia prevention and already monitors people whose blood cell mutations place them at increased risk of developing the disease.

    She added: "At our clinic, we already assess and monitor people who carry blood-cell mutations that increase their risk of leukemia. Today's findings give us real hope of improving how we identify which of them are at greatest risk and point to a window in which prevention could one day be possible.".

    Years of Blood Samples Unlock Newly introduced Cancer Clues.

    A major reason the researchers could reconstruct leukemia's development was the availability of blood samples collected repeatedly from the same individuals over many years.

    Professor Usha Menon of the UCL Institute of Clinical Trials and Methodology, who led the original UKCTOCS project, highlighted the unexpected scientific value of those samples.

    "While UKCTOCS was designed to assess ovarian cancer screening, a key outcome was the establishment of a unique bioresource of serial serum samples. This resource has provided unprecedented opportunities to study how cancers develop over time and to discover and validate biomarkers for earlier detection. We owe an enormous debt of gratitude to the participants whose willingness to contribute their samples and data over many years made this possible. Their generosity is the foundation of this achievement.".

    The women who developed AML received their diagnoses between ages 53 and 83. Because the researchers did not have blood samples taken at the time of diagnosis, they could not directly examine the final stage of the disease's development in those patients.

    The findings also indicated that not every case followed the same extended timeline of detectable changes. In approximately one in five cases, growing populations of mutated blood cells became detectable only one to two years before diagnosis. This suggests that some patients may have a much shorter opportunity for early intervention.

    A Latest Path Toward Preventing Leukemia.

    Despite these limitations, the results offer an encouraging possibility: leukemia risk might be reduced by intervening long before the disease develops.

    According to the researchers' mathematical models, even a modest reduction in the growth of high-risk blood cell clones could have a substantial effect over time. Because these cells multiply exponentially, slowing their expansion across the ten or more years between a second cancer-driving mutation and diagnosis could significantly reduce the likelihood that they eventually progress to leukemia.

    This raises the prospect of preventive treatments designed to restrain dangerous cell populations rather than waiting until they have developed into cancer.

    The next challenge is determining whether such an approach can be used safely and effectively in people identified as having an elevated risk of AML. Although the research provides a promising framework for earlier detection and prevention, clinical studies will be needed to establish whether slowing these abnormal cells actually prevents leukemia in humans.

    The research was primarily supported by UK Research & Innovation and Cancer Research UK.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Along with the Ford Taurus and the Honda Accord, this Toyota is right at the top of the list when Amer­ican families go new-car shopping, and right at the top of the ratings in our last family-sedan comparison test (November 1995).
    • Sources indicate that that won’t change as Toyota introduces its fourth-­generation Camry in Sep­tember, and neither will the mix of virtues that make this model a favorite.
    • See all results for used 1997 Toyota Camry for sale near 94043.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Over 3,000,000 sold! Call it the McCamry. Along with the Ford Taurus and the Honda Accord, this Toyota is right at the top of the list when Amer­ican families go new-car shopping, and right at the top of the ratings in our last family-sedan comparison test (November 1995). Since its introduction here in 1983, Toyota has diligently smoothed up, slicked up, and suaved up the Camry till the only remaining awkwardness is the unlikely spelling of its name.

    Sources indicate that that won’t change as Toyota introduces its fourth-­generation Camry in Sep­tember, and neither will the mix of virtues that make this model a favorite. We’re talking refinement of the Camry theme, not reinvention. In fact, the basic platform and powertrain carry on, though engineering improvements seem to touch every part of the car. It’s slightly bigger in each exterior dimension—0.7 inch longer, 0.4 inch wider, 2.1 inches longer in wheelbase; the same four­-cylinder and V-6 engines are modestly more powerful (up 8 hp in the four, up 6 hp in the V-6); and the interior has been upgraded to meet all the safety standards scheduled in the next few years, including the 1997 side-impact and 1999 head-­impact requirements. The aerodynamic drag coefficient has been improved to 0.30, from 0.33.

    See all results for used 1997 Toyota Camry for sale near 94043.

    Toyota is, however, tightening the Camry’s focus. It’s available only as a four-door now in three trim levels: CE, LE, and XLE. Gone is the coupe, which won over just five percent of Camry buyers. Gone, too, is the station wagon, a shape that convinced only three per­cent of Camry buyers in its losing battle against the tide of minivans. (Production of a Camry-based minivan begins next spring.).

    In the past, we’ve joked that the Camry’s personality is one of aggressive bland­ness. Unlike the frisky feeling of the Accord and the athletic tautness of the Dodge Intrepid, both of which come through loud and clear before you’ve driven to the first corner, the Camry’s subtlety grows on you over time. It’s smoother, softer, quieter than the others, less com­municative, less mechanical. Instead of talking to you in the very pleasant way of those others, it’s the silent type that, you soon notice, goes expertly about its job.

    In a recent development, in this new Camry, Toyota sharpened the expertise without changing the per­sonality. It’s still a car that’s light to the touch: easy to steer, easy to brake. The ride is commendably free of harshness, thanks in part to mounting the suspension on isolated crossmembers front and rear. The four­-cylinder version, with its 195/70SR-14 tires, rides very smoothly and ignores almost completely the road textures that create so much droning in sporting cars. The V-6s come with 205/65HR-15s on six­-inch-wide wheels. These tires are noticeably harsher and noisier than those on the four-cylinder cars, though road nose is still quite reasonable when compared with other cars in this class. Road grip and handling predictability are well above the minimums we’d set for family cars.

    See all results for used 1997 Toyota Camry for sale near 94043.

    In a recent development, the Camry V-6 has been one of the top performers in this class. The 1997 model gains six horsepower (now 194 hp at the same 5200 rpm as the previous peak), gets shorter final-drive gearing (3.93 versus 3.43), and weighs about the same as last year’s smaller car. Another performance plus: A manual transmission has returned to the V-6 lineup, available only on CE models. How­ever, our LE V-6 auto­matic was no quicker than the last LE V-6 we tested, managing 0 to 60 mph in 8.3 seconds. Expect the five-speed to trim that by about four-tenths.

    It has been revealed that on the road, the automatic’s eagerness to change down a gear or two when you press the pedal, even slightly, and the seamless smoothness of those changes give this car quick reflexes in traffic. The engine revs with the hushed moan of a Lexus. This year, traction control is optional on LE and XLE V-6 models. When it comes to powertrain pleasures, the Camry is world-class.

    Recent findings suggest that still, it’s the more subtle details of pas­senger accommodation that make this Toyota a family favorite. In the previous­-generation Camry, our comparison tests show two adults fit in the back seat more comfortably than in some other brands up to 10 inches longer. We expect this Camry advantage to widen fractionally in this latest model because both legroom and head­room in back are increased by a half-inch. Although the Camry is wider on the out­side, energy-absorbing padding to protect in side impacts takes up the extra space and, in certain spots, a little more. The Camry still has pockets in the front doors, unlike the Taurus, which sacrificed them for crash-protection equipment.

    Those who wish to maximize rear-seat space should think twice about opting for power front seats (standard equipment on the top-of-the-line XLE). The manual­adjust buckets have excellent toeroom under them, which the power adjuster interrupts with a transverse bar. Tall folks won’t like that.

    Industry observers note that as in most modern sedans, the Camry has fold-forward rear seatbacks split one­-third and two-thirds, allowing the cargo compartment to be extended into the pas­senger area. Here’s another think-twice: Camrys equipped with the optional child seat—it’s built into the two-thirds section of the rear seat—have that section fixed in place, ruling out all but a narrow passage into the trunk.

    At the rear, the trunklid opens wider and lower than before. Space inside, however, is a bit less in the new body—14.1 cubic feet versus 14.8 before. And the new car still has the conventional trunk hinges with the sickle arms that swing down into your luggage when the lid is closed.

    Sources indicate that conventional is the right description for the new instrument panel, certainly more conventional than the old one, which tried to visually compartmentalize the cockpit by emphasizing a huge black field in front of the driver. That was the good part. The bad part was the deemphasized and totally boring padding it left for the passenger’s amusement. Now the all-new panel stretches its padding across the inte­rior in an equal-opportunity gesture that makes the interior seem brighter and wider. The glove box is 29 percent larger. The audio controls were raised to a mid­dash height, making them easy to see and reach. The climate controls have changed over to the increasingly common turn-to-adjust knobs. They’re large enough, and so obvious in their workings, that they are easy to operate in their less prominent location. The Camry continues to position its ignition switch in the dash where you can readily see it, instead of hiding it on the side of the steering column.

    Sources indicate that toyota has proven itself to be the master of those little conveniences that add up to an exceptionally pleasing car. In this latest Camry we see more clever trade-offs as the engineers cut costs, reduce weight, and usually end up serving the customer better, too. For example, the new front bumper cuts the part count nearly in half and saves weight, yet it increases protec­tion to 5 mph from 2.5. Inside, the seats recline in stepless increments now, and the buckets’ height adjusters use a single knob instead of two. Both of these changes cut costs, Toyota says. We say they make the car better, too. Models that previously would have had retracting antennas now have the antenna screened on the rear glass, saving weight and cost. The new Bosch anti-lock brake system weighs half as much as the old one.

    Sources indicate that still, not every cost saver is a benefit. The LCD odometer is simply gray num­bers on a gray field, making it less visible than the glowing digits in competitors like the Chrysler Cirrus and the Dodge Stratus. And the fresh one-piece front-bumper cover now incorporates the grille into its overtly ordinary Rubbermaid-looking façade.

    There’s been much speculation in the automotive-trade press about a possible price cut. Don’t hold your breath. Sales of the old Camry hit records earlier this year with no apparent price cutting. Were there sweeteners for the dealer? Sure, but other brands had them, too. Toyota knows all the tricks for selling cars without collapsing its price structure-tricks, we think, that mostly won’t be needed to move this shrewdly updated Camry.

    Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.0 brings a latest world, and a Fortnite collaboration

    📅 06 Feb 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (874 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • HoYoverse just wrapped up a substantial Honkai: Star Rail Special Program.
    • Sources indicate that the upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason.
    • According to recent reports, planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    HoYoverse just wrapped up a substantial Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

    Sources indicate that the upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the substantial new world headlining Version 4.0.

    According to recent reports, planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

    The squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

    Industry observers note that the imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

    Industry observers note that the Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

    According to recent reports, much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

    Recent findings suggest that as you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

    Version 4.0 introduces two upcoming 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

    In a recent development, general Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

    According to recent reports, her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

    Recent findings suggest that the other new arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

    It has been revealed that when you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

    She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

    Version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

    Finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the new outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

    It has been revealed that if you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be announced at a later date.

    #121689. Type 2 diabetes linked to 53% higher Alzheimer’s risk, major review finds

    Type 2 diabetes linked to 53% higher Alzheimer’s risk, major review finds

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (389 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Sciencedaily

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that A major research review led by Curtin University has found that people with type 2 diabetes face a significantly higher risk of developing Alzheimer's disease.
    • Recent findings suggest that researchers analyzed data from 40 studies in a systematic review and meta-analysis.
    • A separate analysis found that people with type 2 diabetes had a 53 percent higher adjusted relative risk of developing Alzheimer's compared with those without the condition.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that A major research review led by Curtin University has found that people with type 2 diabetes face a significantly higher risk of developing Alzheimer's disease. The findings provide a clearer picture of the connection between diabetes and Alzheimer's, including how much the risk increases and how frequently new cases occur.

    Recent findings suggest that researchers analyzed data from 40 studies in a systematic review and meta-analysis. They estimated that for every 1,000 people with type 2 diabetes, approximately 4.7 would develop Alzheimer's disease over the course of one year.

    A separate analysis found that people with type 2 diabetes had a 53 percent higher adjusted relative risk of developing Alzheimer's compared with those without the condition.

    Understanding the Link Between Diabetes and Alzheimer's.

    Study author Dr. Emmanuel Adewuyi, an NHMRC Investigator Fellow at the Curtin School of Population Health, explained that the findings offer a more precise understanding of Alzheimer's risk among people with type 2 diabetes.

    Industry observers note that unlike previous research reviews that often examined multiple forms of diabetes or dementia together, this analysis concentrated specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease. It also measured how frequently people with diabetes developed Alzheimer's, providing an additional perspective on the connection between the two conditions.

    "While many earlier reviews combined different types of diabetes or dementia, this review focused specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease and estimated how often new cases occurred," Dr. Adewuyi noted.

    "Relative risk tells us how two groups compare, while incidence tells us how often newly introduced cases occur: putting those numbers together gives us a clearer picture of the burden of Alzheimer's disease among people living with type 2 diabetes.".

    The study, "Incidence and risk of Alzheimer's disease in individuals with type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis," was published in Alzheimer's Research & Therapy.

The eight teams left after the Swiss phase move into a double-elimination bracket played over six competition days, with the playoffs set for 1 to 6 December. The event is listed as an online, A-Tier Riot Games qualifier for 16 teams.

Xora had still reached the Qualifier Playoffs by finishing joint third in the 512-team North America Qualifier 1.

    Recent findings suggest that the organisation’s second line-up had a harder start. Shopify Rebellion Gold lost 0-2 to Maryville University. Several of the other organisations left out of the partnership programme won their first matches. Cloud9 beat counterfeit 2-0, Team Envy beat Yellow Dragon Gaming 2-0 and FlyQuest edged Masterclass 2-1. Elsewhere, Winthrop University beat SaD Esports 2-0 and YFP Gaming beat Wildcard 2-1.

    The prize for coming through the bracket is a place in São Paulo. Riot will stage the 2027 VCT Americas Kickoff in Brazil. Its eight Partner Teams get direct entry. Non-partner teams can win four places: one guaranteed slot each for North America, Brazil and Latin America, plus one for the Americas Last Chance Qualifier. For a non-partner side, a later run to Masters would be worth a fixed US$200,000 and a place at Champions US$400,000, Dot Esports reported. The regional Kickoff events are due to start on 14 January 2027 and run until 7 February 2027.

    #121683. Scientists discover a surprising link between weak bones and faster brain aging

    Scientists discover a surprising link between weak bones and faster brain aging

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1154 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, weakening bones may reveal more about brain health than previously understood.
    • The findings, published in Radiology, a journal of the Radiological Society of North America (RSNA), suggest that bone health and brain aging may be more closely connected than scientists once realized.
    • Bone mineral density reflects how much mineral material, including calcium, is present in a given volume of bone.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, weakening bones may reveal more about brain health than previously understood. A new study from Johns Hopkins University found that people with lower bone density in their spine experienced faster cognitive decline and more rapid deterioration of the brain's white matter as they aged.

    The findings, published in Radiology, a journal of the Radiological Society of North America (RSNA), suggest that bone health and brain aging may be more closely connected than scientists once realized.

    Bone mineral density reflects how much mineral material, including calcium, is present in a given volume of bone. Lower density makes bones more fragile and increases the likelihood of fractures. Although the effects of bone loss on skeletal health are well established, scientists have conducted relatively little research into how declining bone density might relate to changes in the brain.

    Using AI to Investigate Bone Density and Brain Health.

    Sources indicate that to explore this connection, a research team led by Sara Momtazmanesh, M.D., a postdoctoral research fellow in the Department of Radiology and Radiological Sciences at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore, Maryland, examined existing data from the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA). The analysis included information from participants who had undergone chest CT scans without contrast dye, multiple types of brain MRI examinations, and tests measuring cognitive performance.

    Recent findings suggest that the researchers applied a deep learning algorithm developed in the laboratory of Shadpour Demehri, M.D., a Johns Hopkins professor of radiology. The AI system analyzed non-contrast chest CT images from 2,086 MESA participants to determine their initial thoracic vertebral volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD), a measurement of bone density in the spine.

    Of those participants, 715 had the required bone density measurements along with brain MRI results and cognitive testing, making them eligible for the final study group.

    The researchers examined the MRI scans for two indicators of changes in the brain's white matter. The first was white matter hyperintensities, areas of abnormal tissue that appear unusually bright on certain MRI images. The second was reduced fractional anisotropy, a measurement that can indicate deterioration in the microscopic organization of white matter. Both types of changes have been associated with cognitive decline and a greater risk of dementia.

    Follow-up imaging data were available for 408 participants for white matter hyperintensities and 405 participants for fractional anisotropy, allowing researchers to examine how these brain changes progressed over time.

    Lower Bone Density Linked to Faster Cognitive Decline.

    The analysis revealed a notable pattern: participants with lower spinal bone density at the beginning of the study tended to experience a faster decline in overall cognitive performance.

    It has been revealed that the researchers also identified changes in specific brain regions that are crucial for thinking and memory. Lower bone density was associated with greater accumulation of white matter hyperintensities in the corpus callosum, a structure that supports executive function, working memory, and attention.

    Sources indicate that another connection emerged in the anterior limb of the internal capsule, a brain region involved in executive function. Participants with lower bone density highlighted a more pronounced decline in fractional anisotropy in this area, suggesting worsening white matter integrity.

    "This study is the first longitudinal secondary analysis linking baseline vertebral bone mineral density to changes in white matter structure, white matter hyperintensity progression and cognition," Dr. Demehri said. "This comprehensive study using both imaging and clinical assessments sends a clear signal that bone density at baseline is associated with both functional and imaging measures of age-related brain degeneration.".

    Despite the connection between weaker bones and declining brain health, the researchers emphasized that their findings do not establish that osteoporosis causes dementia.

    Instead, bone deterioration and brain degeneration may be consequences of some of the same biological changes that occur with aging.

    According to recent reports, "This study is not about cause and effect, but rather the observation of a metabolic syndrome that may cause both bone and brain degeneration," Dr. Demehri said. "The co-occurrence observed in the study may reflect shared metabolic drivers of aging, including insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, and menopausal change, rather than a direct bone-to-brain effect.".

    Recent findings suggest that these findings raise the possibility that identifying people with reduced bone density could also help recognize those at greater risk of neurological decline. Earlier identification might create opportunities for additional screening and better management of risk factors that affect both skeletal and brain health.

    Routine CT Scans Could Reveal Hidden Signs of Brain Aging.

    One potentially valuable implication of the research is that doctors may be able to obtain useful information about bone density from CT scans that patients have already received for unrelated medical reasons.

    In a recent development, "Chest CT is done for lung cancer screening, calcium scoring, nodule follow-up, and many other indications," Dr. Momtazmanesh noted. "These scans could provide an opportunistic measurement of bone density from the thoracic spine that is associated with a loss of cognitive function.".

    By using AI to analyze existing medical images, researchers may be able to identify patterns of age-related disease that would otherwise go unnoticed. This approach could also help scientists investigate why conditions affecting different parts of the body often develop together.

    Dr. Demehri concurred: "Diagnostic images contain an immense amount of data that AI can now synthesize at scale across multiple organ systems. This creates a robust, newly feasible opportunity to interconnect co-existing age-related pathologies that have traditionally been studied in isolation and to identify shared biological pathways and potential common causal mechanisms.".

    Industry observers note that the study highlights a potentially key connection between bone health and cognitive function, while also demonstrating how AI could make routine medical imaging more informative. Although further research is needed to understand the biological mechanisms involved, the findings suggest that measurements taken from the spine may provide valuable clues about changes occurring in the aging brain.

    In a recent development, the study, "Deep Learning-derived Bone Mineral Density and Longitudinal White Matter Microstructure and Cognitive Decline: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis," also included Quincy A. Hathaway, M.D., Ph.D., Michael P. Bancks, Ph.D., M.P.H., David A. Bluemke, M.D., M.S.B., Ph.D., R. Graham Barr, M.D., Dr.P.H., Wendy S. Post, M.D., M.S., Mohamad Habes, Ph.D., Ilya Nasrallah, M.D., Ph.D., Susan R. Heckbert, M.D., Ph.D., R. Nick Bryan, M.D., Ph.D., Jose A. Luchsinger, M.D., M.P.H., Mei Wan, Ph.D., Matthew Budoff, M.D., João A. C. Lima, M.D., M.B.A., Timothy M. Hughes, Ph.D., M.P.H., and Christos Davatzikos, Ph.D., who collaborated with Drs. Demehri and Momtazmanesh.

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Honda’s bestselling model—and the third-bestselling vehicle in the United States through the third quarter of 2026—is getting a complete makeover.
    • We expect the 2028 CR-V Hybrid to wear a sharp upcoming design, with spy photos showing slim daytime running lights above a series of thin horizontal grilles, while the rear end features a light bar that stretches the full width of the SUV.
    • In a recent development, the cabin is also expected to get a significant makeover, with the Avancier—a three-row SUV sold in Asia—providing hints about what to expect.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Honda’s bestselling model—and the third-bestselling vehicle in the United States through the third quarter of 2026—is getting a complete makeover. The CR-V will follow the path set forth by the sixth-generation Toyota RAV4, going hybrid only as the CR-V enters its seventh generation for the 2028 model year.

    We expect the 2028 CR-V Hybrid to wear a sharp upcoming design, with spy photos showing slim daytime running lights above a series of thin horizontal grilles, while the rear end features a light bar that stretches the full width of the SUV. It will likely also be the first vehicle in the U.S. to wear Honda’s new “H” logo, which was originally introduced for its future EVs but will now be applied to other vehicles in its lineup after Honda hurriedly canceled said EVs earlier this year.

    In a recent development, the cabin is also expected to get a significant makeover, with the Avancier—a three-row SUV sold in Asia—providing hints about what to expect. The Avancier skips out on most real buttons and knobs, instead putting nearly every function into a large screen mounted to the dashboard, a dramatic shift from Honda’s current setup that prioritizes physical controls. The Avancier’s interior is wrapped in white upholstery, accented by glowing ambient lighting, and features a squared-off steering wheel. Honda also appears to be switching to a column-mounted gear selector.

    See all results for upcoming 2028 Honda CR-V Hybrid for sale near 19701.

    While Honda was once led by the Accord and Civic sedans, in today’s SUV-obsessed market, the CR-V has become the Japanese automaker’s most notable model. Its biggest rival, the RAV4, was overhauled for 2026 and went hybrid only. Now, the CR-V will follow suit to stay competitive in the incredibly crowded compact SUV segment. Hybrid sales of the current-generation CR-V have been strong, accounting for over half of the SUV’s total sales so far this year, making it a perfect choice to launch Honda’s new platform and hybrid powertrain.

    It has been revealed that the CR-V will arrive on a newly introduced platform that Honda promises will be stiffer and lighter than before, taking a modular approach that will lead to greater parts sharing and reducing costs. This platform will presumably be adapted to underpin future versions of the Accord and Civic, along with Acura models such as the upcoming next-generation RDX Hybrid.

    Recent findings suggest that honda will ditch the standard 190-hp 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine for the 2028 CR-V, which will arrive exclusively with the organization’s new hybrid powertrain. The fifth generation of Honda’s two-motor hybrid setup will continue to use an Atkinson-cycle four-cylinder, along with a pair of electric motors, but the 2.0-liter engine will be a fresh design, featuring a new cooling system. As before, the electric motors will power the wheels most of the time, but the gas engine can also be engaged to directly drive the wheels.

    See all results for upcoming 2028 Honda CR-V Hybrid for sale near 19701.

    Industry observers note that the electric motors are more compact than before, and Honda has developed a latest battery too. The manufacturer says the new hybrid setup will bring improved power and efficiency, targeting 10 percent better fuel economy than the outgoing hybrid powertrain. The current CR-V Hybrid makes 205 horsepower and is rated at up to 38 mpg combined. We wouldn’t be surprised to see power increase to over 220 hp—the RAV4 makes 226 hp in FWD form and 236 hp with AWD—and fuel economy nudge up to just over 40 mpg.

    The CR-V is expected to come with front-wheel drive standard and all-wheel drive optional, although it’s unclear if the latter will see the addition of a third electric motor. Honda will also likely include the S+ Shift feature seen on the Civic Hybrid and Prelude, which simulates a traditional transmission’s gearchanges and allows the driver to manually shift with the steering-wheel paddles.

    The CR-V’s chief rival will continue to be the Toyota RAV4. However, the Hyundai Tucson Hybrid and Nissan Rogue Hybrid, which both enter a new generation for 2027, will also be strong competitors. The Jeep Cherokee, Kia Sportage Hybrid, and Subaru Forester Hybrid will be in the mix too, along with nonhybrid compact SUVs like the Volkswagen Tiguan.

    The move to only offer a hybrid powertrain could see the CR-V’s entry price climb, which might alienate some buyers. Honda will also need to make sure it can match or exceed the efficiency of rivals like the RAV4 while still providing adequate performance and a spacious, usable cabin, given how closely matched the compact SUV space is these days. Moving away from physical interior controls could also upset the Honda faithful who are used to the manufacturer’s simple-to-use buttons.

    Production is set to kick off at Honda’s factories in East Liberty, Ohio, and Greensburg, Indiana, in April 2027. Sales should begin shortly after, and with the current CR-V Hybrid starting at $37,580, we expect the next-generation model to come in at around $38,000.

WARDOGS and Movember have teamed up for the chilly month of November for a mental health collab to raise awareness about men’s health and mental health. It’s time to give a virtual hand to your teammates on and off the battlefield while you keep earning coin.

    Until November 30th, you’ll be able to keep your upper lip warmer (over the ski mask) as you shoot your way out of hairy situations with the Movember Pack DLC.

    Just like it’s crucial to check on your teammates, it’s a good time to check on your mates as well. Drop by, send a message, see how they’re doing with everything going on in the world; it’s better to join forces and fight missions together with maximum health possible, after all.

    Players who take part in this charity drive also get a badge called the November 2026 Scoreboard Badge, which is permanent to show that they participated in the men’s health event.

    Unfortunately, the stache itself only is available to use during November, as does the Movember event only exist in November, but that doesn’t mean that one should only check on his pals during one month a year.

    Many things can happen to one’s friends, and prevention remains the best weapon in the game, with both mental health and screenings for prostate and testicular cancer.

    According to recent reports, we all have different methods of how to ease up, and for many men, it is gaming. Multiplayer titles in particular are great to unite with buddies after a long day at work or during some downtime at the weekend.

    Sometimes just talking to a friend while multitasking with a controller can do wonders for mental health, on top of pushing away the loneliness.

    Just like a real stache, it starts small but keeps growing with the player using it.

Rep your moustaches with your mates as another community cosmetic to show how handsome all you lads are.

    #121676. Depression may be an early warning sign of Alzheimer's disease

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (548 w)

    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

    Depression may be an early warning sign of Alzheimer's disease

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (548 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that changes in mood later in life may offer key clues about what is happening inside the brain, even before problems with memory or thinking become noticeable.
    • It has been revealed that the study, published in JNeurosci, was conducted by Teodora Markova of Brandeis University and her colleagues.
    • Alzheimer's Protein Linked to Worsening Depression.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that changes in mood later in life may offer key clues about what is happening inside the brain, even before problems with memory or thinking become noticeable. Fresh research suggests that the buildup of tau, a protein closely associated with Alzheimer's disease, may contribute to worsening depressive symptoms in older adults.

    It has been revealed that the study, published in JNeurosci, was conducted by Teodora Markova of Brandeis University and her colleagues. The team investigated how tau levels relate to depression during normal aging and in people experiencing the cognitive (memory, attention, and thinking) difficulties associated with Alzheimer's disease.

    Alzheimer's Protein Linked to Worsening Depression.

    It has been revealed that to investigate this connection, researchers analyzed information from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, a research project that tracks changes in brain health over time. The data included older men and women, some with cognitive difficulties and others whose memory and thinking abilities remained intact.

    Participants underwent multiple brain scans designed to detect tau accumulation and completed questionnaires assessing depressive symptoms at different points during the study. This allowed researchers to examine how changes in tau levels corresponded with changes in mood over time.

    According to recent reports, among participants with normal cognitive abilities, the researchers discovered a striking pattern. Those whose tau levels increased more rapidly also tended to experience a faster rise in depressive symptoms. Higher tau levels also helped predict more severe depressive symptoms in these individuals.

    The results suggest that tau may begin influencing mood before measurable cognitive problems emerge. However, the same relationships were not observed among participants who already had mild cognitive impairment or Alzheimer's disease.

    Could Depression Reveal Early Brain Changes?

    Recent findings suggest that the findings suggest that tau accumulation during the early stages of brain aging may contribute to the development or worsening of depression. They also raise the possibility that changes in mood could provide useful information about brain health before memory loss becomes apparent.

    Researchers believe that following depressive symptoms over time, alongside other assessments, could eventually help identify older adults who may be at greater risk of developing neurodegenerative diseases. However, additional research is needed to establish whether these early changes in mood can reliably predict future cognitive decline.

    Markova emphasized the importance of studying these relationships over longer periods, particularly as some participants develop more noticeable depression or begin experiencing cognitive difficulties.

    "Future work can continue to track how participants' tau levels and depression symptoms evolve over longer periods of time, particularly as some develop cognitive impairment or more clinically significant levels of depression. Continuing to follow these trajectories, observing how early mood changes relate to later clinical outcomes, and establishing relationships with other methods tracking the development of Alzheimer's disease will provide more clarity on methods to determine which individuals may be at an increased risk.".

    Materials provided by Society for Neuroscience. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

    Latest Update: 10 Fun 2026 Games That Would Make for Great Holiday Gifts

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1525 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • For many cultures and countries across the globe, the holiday season is in full swing, with many households preparing to attend family gatherings, celebrate events, and, of course, starting to purchase holiday gifts for children and other loved ones.
    • Several storefronts and digital retailers have already begun issuing early Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals, with many products, especially physical video games, going on sale for 25-50% off their original sale price.
    • With 2026 being a particularly great year for fresh video game releases, here are 10 fun new video games that were released this year that would make for great holiday gifts for loved ones of all kinds ranging from titles intended for children to those aimed at more mature gamers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    For many cultures and countries across the globe, the holiday season is in full swing, with many households preparing to attend family gatherings, celebrate events, and, of course, starting to purchase holiday gifts for children and other loved ones.

    Several storefronts and digital retailers have already begun issuing early Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals, with many products, especially physical video games, going on sale for 25-50% off their original sale price.

    With 2026 being a particularly great year for fresh video game releases, here are 10 fun new video games that were released this year that would make for great holiday gifts for loved ones of all kinds ranging from titles intended for children to those aimed at more mature gamers.

    According to recent reports, mojang’s Minecraft is considered by gamers of all ages to be one of the greatest games of all time, and over the years it’s been expanded upon through numerous updates. If fans want to get an early look at the game’s first newly introduced dimension in 15 years, then they’ll have to check out Minecraft Dungeons II.

    In a recent development, like its 2020 predecessor, Minecraft Dungeons II is a third-person hack and slash dungeon crawler. It follows a hero as they set out to stop illagers from threatening the world with power from the new Warden-based Sift dimension, fighting a variety of new exclusive mobs along the way.

    While Minecraft Dungeons II has only been out for less than two months so far and isn’t at the moment on sale, it would surely make a great holiday gift for any fan of Minecraft, especially kids, as it does feature local four-player co-op allowing siblings, parents, and friends to easily play together.

    It has been revealed that avengers: Doomsday is expected to be the biggest movie release of the decade. While Marvel fans still have to wait till late December to see the film, they can quench their thirst for action-packed Marvel content by purchasing Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls.

    Set in the Japanese anime-inspired Earth-358, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is a 2D 4v4 tag team fighting game centered around the Fighting Avengers, the Unbreakable X-Men, the Amazing Guardians, the Samurai Outriders, and the Knights of Doom fighting each other to ultimately defeat the Champion of the Universe.

    Industry observers note that marvel Tokon is easily the best Marvel video game released this year. Not only does it feature over 20 playable heroes and villains, but it also includes five distinct campaigns following each team attempting to defeat the Champion, with the best arguably following Doctor Doom and his cadre of iconic villains.

    In a recent development, 2026 has been great for horror titles, as fantastic games like The Sinking City 2 and Resident Evil Requiem debuted earlier this year. However, I would argue that the best horror game to gift horror fans this holiday season is Tarsier Studios’ Reanimal.

    Similar in gameplay and visual design to the Little Nightmares series, Reanimal is a co-op platforming survival horror game following a young brother and sister as they travel to their home island to find three friends. Tragically, they find it in ruins and filled with gigantic humanoid and animalistic monsters.

    Some horror stories are best experienced alone, but Reanimal is one that family and friends alike will certainly enjoy playing through together as they tackle puzzles and try to solve the mystery surrounding the island and its inhabitants.

    Millions of fans around the world love Star Wars. While Disney is releasing a ton of different SW products this holiday season to tantalize shoppers, people should consider gifting their Star Wars and video game fan loved ones with the surprise hit, Star Wars: Galactic Racer.

    A roguelite racing game set shortly after the Battle of Jakku, Star Wars: Galactic Racer is centered around the rise of unsanctioned races via the fresh Galactic Racing League, with the protagonist Shade attempting to become the new Galactic League champion.

    According to recent reports, galactic Racer’s colorful cast of characters and intense races utilizing podracers, land speeders, speeder bikes, or skim speeders have swiftly made it become one of the most critically acclaimed SW titles in years. Fans will surely fall in love with the game for the hilarious character of Biddy Blas alone.

    LEGO products have become a signature gift for decades now. While many parents will undoubtedly buy their kids a few LEGO sets this holiday season, they should also consider buying them the LEGO video game, LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight.

    Unlike past TT LEGO titles, LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight isn’t based on any particular Batman movie but is rather a conglomeration of all things Batman, utilizing a gameplay structure similar to Batman: Arkham Knight while using elements from several Batman films, comics, and demonstrates.

    Legacy may not feature as many playable characters as past TT games, but it more than makes up for it by featuring dozens of alternate costumes for each character, alternate driveable variations of the Batmobile, and a customizable Batcave on top of returning two-player co-op.

    According to recent reports, some gamers enjoy first-person shooters while others enjoy simulators, but some players want more open-world, narrative-driven experiences such as those commonly found in role-playing games. Arguably the best RPG of 2026 is Rebel Wolves’ debut title, The Blood of Dawnwalker.

    Made by the creators of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, The Blood of Dawnwalker is a medieval fantasy RPG set in the 14th century kingdom of Vale Sangora, following a half-man half-vampire named Coen as he sets out to save his family and his country from the clutches of the Ancient Roman vampire Brencis.

    The story, characters, and world-building of Dawnwalker are absolutely incredible, but it also has a ton of replay value as players can invest in witchcraft, sword skills, or vampire abilities and even accidentally drain the blood of NPCs if they don’t maintain their vampiric thirst.

    Many older gamers are more action-oriented, and while 2026 has seen many great action games come out over the past few months, like Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, I would argue that best action game to gift gamers this holiday season is Gears of War: E-Day.

    The sixth mainline entry in the third-person Gears of War series and prequel to the first Gears game, Gears of War: E-Day follows COG soldiers Marcus Fenix, Dominic Santiago, Mags Carter, and Lucas Reyes as they struggle to fight a horrifying invasion from the subterranean Locust Horde on Emergence Day.

    E-Day may only be available on PC and Xbox Series X|S consoles, but it's by far the best Xbox exclusive released in years thanks to its gruesome, action-packed, yet emotional co-op campaign, thrilling PvP multiplayer, and addictive PvE Horde Siege mode.

    With Legendary Pictures and Toho releasing several great Godzilla movies in recent years, many kids are growing up as huge Godzilla fans. A perfect gift to get them this holiday season is Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered.

    A remaster of 2002’s Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is a four-player 3D fighting game with players being able to control some of Toho's most famous kaiju in city-destroying battles. Such behemoths as Godzilla, Rodan, King Ghidorah, Mechagodzilla, and more are playable.

    What makes Godzilla: DAMMR an especially great gift this holiday season is its affordable price and small file size, with the game currently being sold on PS5 for $29.99 and featuring a file size of about 5 GB, making it a quick game to download and start playing.

    According to recent reports, similar to LEGO, Pokemon has increasingly become a prevalent presence in households during the holiday season. While there are several Pokemon products to gift people this season, I would recommend people gift Pokemon Pokopia to fans.

    Unlike the main turn-based RPG games, Pokemon Pokopia is social simulation game akin to Animal Crossing, with players embodying a human-imitating Ditto waking up in a post-apocalyptic version of the Kanto region and setting out to restore the area using its transformative powers.

    What follows is an adorably charming experience as Ditto rebuilds habitats and befriends Pokemon from every generation, with people even able to create their own structures and minigames similar to Minecraft to play with friends.

    One of the best games to gift anyone this holiday season is undoubtedly the 2026 masterpiece that is The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for the Nintendo Switch 2.

    Released to celebrate The Legend of Zelda’s 40th anniversary, 2026’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a faithful modern remake of the classic Nintendo 64 action-adventure game, with the game once again following a young Link as he set out to save the kingdom of Hyrule from the evil Ganondorf.

    Being a first-party Nintendo game that’s only a few weeks old, it’s unlikely that the Ocarina of Time remake will go on sale anytime soon, but it’s well worth purchasing at full price. Especially for parents who want to introduce their kids to Link’s most famous adventure for the first time.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch. The game’s second season was delayed in mid-January, and the developer even brought back Battlefield Labs to test out some of the fresh content and features coming with the new season.

    Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a new blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing concerns with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.

    Recent findings suggest that we know that Season 2 is introducing a substantial latest map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing. The map will indeed arrive in the first part of the season, and it’s going to do so alongside a new LTM that “introduces a new element of tactics.” A second, “high-intensity map” will debut later into the season, alongside another LTM where players battle through an underground base, in darkness.

    Sources indicate that the real meat of the blog post, however, covers the broader gameplay changes everyone will see once the new season kicks off. There’s a massive focus on player progression, especially when it concerns free-to-play Redsec players.

    Challenges are being streamlined yet again, with more broad parameters that don’t require specific modes. Some, like dailies, will also allow for assists to count towards their criteria. Less restrictive challenges are welcome, but even more so is the faster battle pass progression.

    BF Studios is changing the rate at which battle pass Tokens are earned from career XP, and making it so they’re earnable by playing the game normally, and by completing weekly challenges. These changes should also help Redsec players, who will also benefit from faster career and weapon XP earn rates - across both battle royale, and Gauntlet. In general, the career experience should feel more rewarding, especially for earlier ranks.

    Weapon balance and recoil are two areas that will continue to evolve in Battlefield 6, it seems, and Season 2 is specifically tackling recoil patterns to make them more consistent when you compensate for them.

    According to recent reports, movement is being adjusted with the Season 2 patch, too, though thankfully it’s limited to general feel that touches areas like vaulting, ladder transitions, and acceleration curves. You should also see better continuity and consistency between animations and feel.

    Industry observers note that audio is getting a pass with the upcoming patch, especially when it comes to footstep and interaction audio. This also extends to something the developer has been working on improving for a while, and it has to do with how the game decides which audio tracks to prioritise in busy situations.

    Tomorrow, the full Battlefield 6 Season 2 trailer will be released, while a more detailed roadmap is expected by the end of this week.

    #121667. Strange new materials can crawl, walk, and dig like living creatures

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1207 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

    Strange new materials can crawl, walk, and dig like living creatures

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1207 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Most materials simply react when something pushes, pulls, or bends them.
    • According to recent reports, everyday materials such as metal, concrete, glass, and rubber are generally considered passive.
    • It contains an internal source of energy that allows it to respond to its surroundings in ways ordinary materials cannot.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Most materials simply react when something pushes, pulls, or bends them. But a very different category of matter can draw on its own energy to change shape and respond to outside forces in surprising ways. Known as active matter, these unusual materials are attracting growing scientific interest. Now, physicists from the universities of Amsterdam, Latest South Wales, and Cambridge have uncovered remarkable new behaviors that could change how future machines and robots are designed.

    According to recent reports, everyday materials such as metal, concrete, glass, and rubber are generally considered passive. They can stretch, bend, shift, or change shape when forces act on them, but the energy needed to produce those changes comes from outside the material.

    Active matter works differently. It contains an internal source of energy that allows it to respond to its surroundings in ways ordinary materials cannot. Many examples occur naturally in living systems. A flock of birds, for instance, can move together as a coordinated group, adjusting its behavior in response to wind, changes in the landscape, available food, or a suitable place to rest.

    Scientists can also recreate some of these remarkable properties in the laboratory. Researchers from the University of Amsterdam (The Netherlands), the University of Cambridge (UK), and the University of New South Wales (Sydney, Australia) have spent several years developing active materials from surprisingly simple components, including miniature motors, rods, and rubber bands. Their experiments have revealed unusual mechanical behaviors with potentially valuable applications, leading to two recently accepted scientific papers.

    Scientists Create Materials That Can Crawl, Walk, and Dig.

    One of the discoveries involves two familiar mechanical behaviors known as buckling and snapping.

    It has been revealed that imagine squeezing a paper ticket between your fingers. As the pressure increases, the ticket becomes unstable and bends to one side. If you then press against the curved surface, it initially pushes back before suddenly flipping in the opposite direction.

    Industry observers note that this is how ordinary passive materials behave. External forces supply the energy needed for the ticket to buckle and snap, and each action occurs only once in response to the applied force.

    Recent findings suggest that the researchers discovered that adding internal activity can fundamentally transform this behavior. They assembled a series of connected rods into a flexible chain, placing small motors at the joints where neighboring rods meet. These motors created interactions that were not symmetrical. Moving one rod could affect its neighbor in a different way than moving that neighbor would affect the original rod (by rotating over a different angle, for example).

    The result was striking. When external forces acted on these active chains, they still bent and snapped, but the movement no longer had to end after a single event. Instead, the structures could repeatedly buckle and snap, producing ongoing oscillations.

    The underlying physics involves a transformation of the system's critical point, where snapping normally takes place, into what researchers call a critical exceptional point. This unusual behavior makes it possible for the chains to generate movements resembling crawling, walking, and even digging.

    Industry observers note that the findings were published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, with Sami Al-Izzi of the University of New South Wales and Yao Du of the University of Amsterdam serving as joint first authors. One of the team's buckling chains was also featured on the journal's cover.

    Industry observers note that beyond revealing unexpected physics, the discovery points toward a promising approach to building materials capable of performing multiple tasks autonomously. Such structures could be especially useful in flexible, "soft" robots, potentially allowing their bodies to produce complex movements without relying on a centralized control system.

    Active Matter Challenges a Fundamental Engineering Principle.

    A separate investigation by the same international research team uncovered another surprising property of active materials, this time challenging a principle widely used in engineering.

    Whether designing large bridges or tiny nanomechanical devices, engineers depend on established rules that connect the properties of individual components to the behavior of an entire structure.

    It has been revealed that one such rule is Le Chatelier's Principle. In the mechanical context described by the researchers, it suggests that changes made to individual parts of a system should produce corresponding changes in the overall structure. For example, making a structure's individual components stiffer would generally be expected to increase the stiffness of the entire assembly.

    Recent findings suggest that but the researchers found that active matter does not always follow this expectation. In some cases, increasing the activity of individual components can actually reduce the activity of the material as a whole.

    To investigate this counterintuitive effect, the scientists built another structure using motors and rods. Rather than arranging the components in a chain, they connected them into a flat, two-dimensional network resembling a lattice. They then examined how the elastic behavior of the entire structure changed depending on the properties of its individual elements.

    Their experiments revealed that the overall response depended on more than simply how active each component was. What mattered was whether the active elements formed connected pathways capable of transmitting mechanical responses throughout the structure.

    Why More Activity Can Produce Less Response.

    The researchers identified a process called percolation as the key to understanding this unexpected behavior.

    According to recent reports, A useful comparison is the movement of water through ground coffee. If the coffee grounds are packed too tightly, water cannot easily travel through the entire layer. The arrangement of the grounds determines whether the water can find a continuous path.

    Something similar happens inside active materials. If too many of the interconnected components have relatively low activity, they can prevent elastic responses from spreading through the structure. Even when other components are extremely active, their influence may not extend across the entire material.

    Sources indicate that this explains why making some parts more active does not necessarily produce a more active structure overall. The way the components are connected and distributed can be just as vital as their individual properties.

    The second study, led by first author Jack Binysh from Corentin Coulais's research group at the University of Amsterdam, was published in Physical Review X.

    Sources indicate that the researchers believe that this unexpected departure from Le Chatelier's Principle could have notable implications for understanding and designing systems built from active microscopic structures. These include biological gels, epithelial monolayers, which are sheets of closely connected cells, and neuromorphic networks that mimic aspects of biological information processing.

    In a recent development, together, the findings reveal how dramatically materials can behave when their internal components actively consume energy and interact in unconventional ways. The discoveries could influence research across physics, soft matter science, mechanical engineering, the life sciences, and robotics, while opening fresh possibilities for creating adaptable materials and smarter robotic systems.

    Materials provided by Universiteit van Amsterdam. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

    Alongside the MENA winner, Europe sends two qualifiers to Berlin and Türkiye sends one. The partner teams already in the field are BBL Esports, Fnatic, FUT Esports, Gentle Mates, Karmine Corp, Team Heretics, Team Liquid and Team Vitality. Fnatic were confirmed in October 2026 as staying on as a VCT EMEA partner for 2027.

    Recent findings suggest that the tournament will be played in person at the Riot Games Arena in Berlin in early 2027. For the MENA winner, the trip carries direct financial value. Riot’s support for non-partner teams starts at Kickoff, and the sums rise for teams that progress further through the season.

    In a recent development, non-partner teams that qualify for Masters receive US$200,000, and those reaching Champions receive US$400,000, Dot Esports reported. Europe’s route to Kickoff runs in parallel. The Europe Kickoff Qualifier Playoffs begin with a Swiss stage from 25 to 29 November, followed by playoffs from 3 to 5 December.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Everything is Crab is a roguelite evolution game where you start off as a blob, needing to eat to upgrade yourself and learn to survive! There are some base-level stats that you can start with, sometimes making you a bit more than a blob, but you'll still need to come a long way if you want to survive in the harsh world around you.

    It has been revealed that the map itself is interesting, with areas of snow, rain, and desert. These areas can affect your blob, freezing you or slowing you down as you move through the sand. There are some foods along the ground in the form of fruits, but mainly you can beat up smaller creatures and bugs so that you can eat their flesh. This fills up a bar at the bottom of the screen that then allows you to evolve!

    According to recent reports, when you evolve, you can pick one of three upgrades that appear, some of which help you eat faster or ones that change the way you look physically, or ones that upgrade evolutions you have previously made. There are some that give you bigger attacks or change the way that you dash away. It's quite fun to see the combination that you end up with and how they all gel together. Though, these evolutions are worth reading through because sometimes they have less-than-desirable effects that pair with them.

    As you continue to grow and evolve in Everything is Crab, there is also a timeline on the top of the screen. This reveals moments when bosses will appear, who will trap you in a giant fenced area. You will then need to beat up this boss, as they will continue to chase you around until you've died. One giant spider guy actually started dropping web pods that released more spiders - it was quite the undertaking! Defeating bosses does give you DNA strips, which can be used to re-roll your evolutions or to upgrade your evolutions so that they do double the increase that you want to pick.

    In a recent development, there are some areas that you can discover, represented by a question mark on your map. These little interaction points give you three options to choose from, primarily at tiny trees or at giant mushrooms, which change how you interact with mushrooms in other places on the map. There are also places where you can hide, though that wastes time!

    Slowly, through doing more and more of these runs, you will unlock new ways of playing, like different difficulties or starting points for your blob, which continue to make the game more interesting. I like the size and pacing of these runs, which do save, so you do not need to do them all at once. I do find that sometimes the UI overlaps itself on my mobile phone, which can be a little strange, but you are still able to read everything anyway.

    Industry observers note that download now! Everything is Crab.
