    #121549. Latest Update: Opinion: After Finishing Ocarina Of Time, I'm Left Jonesing For A Proper Sequel

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (996 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nintendolife ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Opinion: After Finishing Ocarina Of Time, I'm Left Jonesing For A Proper Sequel

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (996 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nintendolife

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Yesterday I finished the Ocarina of Time remake.
    • It's an excellent video game, a thoroughly impressive revamp which changes enough to feel modern without trampling over the original.
    • Industry observers note that still, after catching the Loach and using the in-game menus to track down the last Skulltulas and Heart Pieces — and even dipping into Zelda Notes and OCD-ing every last rupee-filled Treasure Chest for the magic 100% rating in the app — I was left feeling a tad...deflated?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Yesterday I finished the Ocarina of Time remake. Having replayed the original over the summer with my kids, we've beansed it through this one, taking our time to enjoy the view and appreciate the myriad changes, but already knowing exactly where to go and what to do.

    What is there left to say about it? It's an excellent video game, a thoroughly impressive revamp which changes enough to feel modern without trampling over the original. I have a handful of tiny issues with it (the Sheik reveal always felt a bit obvious, but here I don't see how anybody won't see it coming), but they're minuscule in the scheme of things. Childhoods haven't been ruined, and at a time when genuine warm fuzzies are in short supply, Nintendo has delivered.

    Industry observers note that still, after catching the Loach and using the in-game menus to track down the last Skulltulas and Heart Pieces — and even dipping into Zelda Notes and OCD-ing every last rupee-filled Treasure Chest for the magic 100% rating in the app — I was left feeling a tad...deflated? That's not quite the word, but there was an emptiness.

    It's a stunning game and I enjoyed every second, but as a remake it naturally lacked the same sense of wonder you get from exploring and not knowing what's around the next corner. Delight up the wazoo, but not so much in the 'surprise' department.

    According to recent reports, the natural conclusion, given the very warm reception and impressive sales, is that Nintendo will crack straight on with Majora's Mask next. And yes, absolutely; MM is my personal favourite, so of course I'll take a remake. It's the least-brainer-y no-brainer since Ocarina 3D was a hit.

    However, already knowing the world and the story does take something away from the Zelda experience, and having now appreciated this remake's gorgeous art style, the presentation would provide less novelty next time, too.

    Industry observers note that "It's not as exciting when you know what's coming," said my seven-year-old last night after we rolled credits. Both kids still sat beside me for "30 hours or more" over the past three weeks, mind, so let's not blow this out of proportion. I could feel her attention wandering at times, though, even with the grandeur of the visuals and all the additions.

    So, I've now got a dilemma. Do I show them the original Majora's Mask as planned, or wait for the hypothetical remake and preserve its narrative twists and turns? Would they prefer to be surprised? Despite wanting to see the Zora mask in action, they'd both rather wait. Saying they'll be old enough to control it themselves in a couple of years may have soured them on watching me play the "square-y" version now. Fingers crossed Nintendo actually makes the thing.

    The parent's perspective isn't a consideration for everyone, it's just an interesting conundrum. I'm also aware that none of this is an concern for Ocarina newbies! For me personally, though, as much as I would/will devour Majora's Mask, there's another approach that could bring the best of both worlds. A link, ahem, between worlds, if you will. What about a brand latest sequel to Ocarina?

    Sources indicate that imagine a game which continues the Hero of Time's journey, with Link grown up — in his mid-20s, say — exploring a Hyrule changed by his heroics in the first game. This Link saved Hyrule and Termina, and (almost) nobody in his world knows it. That's fertile ground for a story only hinted at in Twilight Princess.

    The Ocarina remake gives glimpses of a larger world beyond Hyrule's hills. How about a sequel that lets us explore those, expanding the horizons and pushing out the frontiers of this contained kingdom? A game which taps our emotional connections and nostalgia but brings something truly unknown as well.

    Could that be it? Could that integration of old and fresh — Ocarina + BOTW — be a direction for the series as a whole? Mashing two known ideas to make something notionally fresh is fandom 101, of course. "What if Ocarina but bigger?" "What if old Link travelled back with a warning!" "What if Dark Link was a premonition and the Hero of Time has to save Hyrule from his own ego!" It's easy to pump out the 'what ifs'.

    It's also easy to say, "Oh, just put old-school Ocarina-like dungeons into the open world!" It's a design headache, to be sure, but also a problem Nintendo has the know-how to tackle.

    It has been revealed that I just feel like there's more gold to mine from this world and this engine beyond a straightforward Majora's Mask remake. I'd play that and love it, the same as if they unveiled A Link to the Past or a reimagined version of the NES original. But I have played those games already - a vital element of the Zelda formula is missing in any remake.

    Sources indicate that not feeling like a 'stopgap' project to train up staff while Aonuma and co. work out how the hell to follow up Tears of the Kingdom is one of this remake's most impressive qualities. We've already asked the question about whether that open-world Hyrule could withstand a third entry, and a direct sequel to TOTK seems unlikely. In some ways, remaking The Best Game of All Time was a mighty clever distraction.

    Recent findings suggest that however, if Nintendo doesn't have some revolutionary upcoming take on Zelda up its sleeve just yet, I'd love to see them exploit this Hyrule and explore this Link's story some more. The last time they told a new story with a Link from long ago, we got the sublime A Link Between Worlds. Yes. Yes, please.

    Let us know below how you'd feel about more adventures in strange new (and old) worlds with the Hero of Time, whether that's revisiting Termina or something else entirely.

    • The game was originally revealed by NEKCOM back in January 2022, known as Project SAS.
    • Sources indicate that the announcement was made through NEKCOM’s social media, where they confirmed the official launch for October 28, 2027.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you were feeling like today was a good day for killing some zombies in a Japanese-American setting as a teenage girl brought back from the dead, this might not be a happy day for you, as Showa American Story has been pushed back for a later release.

    The game was originally revealed by NEKCOM back in January 2022, known as Project SAS. While it had no initial release date, the game was later unveiled (now with its proper name) for the PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, and Steam. As production went on, the team had to let go of the former version, and after some more delays, it’s now projected to come out officially in 2027.

    Sources indicate that the announcement was made through NEKCOM’s social media, where they confirmed the official launch for October 28, 2027. The announcement reaffirms the team’s focus on “polishing and optimizing the experience” for the title before its official release. This has been a frequent move by developers over the last few years, and probably for the best.

    Industry observers note that notable titles that went through the same way include Assassin’s Creed Shadows, Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, and, of course, GTA 6, which all took some extra time to guarantee a perfectly-tuned experience for the players. And with so many Easter eggs and secrets to discover in some of those games, it’s hard to say this was a bad call.

    Sources indicate that showa American Story had its release date first revealed back in 2024, projected for a 2025 window. However, the game was pushed back to 2026 to ensure its development would go smoothly. And while it’s now being pushed back once again, we can probably rest assured that this should be the last time, as it now has a fixed date for its release.

    The announcement reaffirms the team’s focus on ‘polishing and optimizing the experience’ for the title before its official release.

    It has been revealed that the Chinese RPG game was first conceptualized back in 2016, but only entered official development during this decade. It follows an alternative timeline where the United States has been heavily influenced by Japan, bringing a chaotic amalgamation of cultures to life. Oh, and we have zombies too.

    We follow the story of Chigusa Choko, a 19-year-old stuntwoman who has been brought back to life alongside hordes of undead. After awakening years after her death, in the so-called Showa era 66, Choko is looking for answers to why she is back in this period, and what has transpired to make the world fall into such disorder. It’s just your average zombie movie, but with some interesting quirks.

    A good example is how Choko has some kind of unique power. Her physical capacities are greatly enhanced, and she can easily make her way through the waves of mindlessly acting bodies. But with a lot of gore, of course. From melee weapons to heavy gunfire, she has tons of ways to make quick work of her fellow undead.

    But the main attraction here is the amazing “Showa America” culture, combining both of the best and the worst aspects of the Showa Era in Japan and our ever-loving American Dream in one. The 80s and 90s culture of both countries is presented as one, so it’s not uncommon to catch one of the other survivors in this apocalyptic setting to gush over their favorite anime right after saluting their flag.

    With your usual amount of special moves coming straight out of a B-movie, plenty of dark humor, and a lot of love for both the represented cultures, Showa American Story is definitely a title I’m excited to hear more about. And as the industry grows ever so demanding, I’m glad to see it’ll have some extra time to cook. It's done wonders for GTA, so I can’t complain about it now.

As if that wasn’t enough, now Cal Kestis’ actor is back talking about the role and potentially even teasing another game.

    Recent findings suggest that earlier this week, the official Star Wars Twitter account shared a surprise video where Cal Kestis actor Cameron Monaghan delivers a message to Ashoka’s Ezra Bridger, Eman Esfandi. The video is really just a cute nod to Esfandi playing through Jedi: Fallen Order, but there are some interesting levels to it.

    As the comments point out, it’s a little suspicious in the first place that Monaghan is suddenly talking about Cal Kestis and Star Wars Jedi for the first time in a long while. The background of the video he’s in is clearly shot somewhere to do with Star Wars (likely Galaxy’s Edge), which suggests he’s not been far from Lucasfilm.

    That’s already enough to get everyone thinking about Jedi 3’s impending reveal, but Monaghan’s intro is also interesting. He says that he plays Cal Kestis in “Jedi: Survivor and Jedi: Fallen Order”, the only two games to release so far, before also saying, “and the Jedi games”, despite there being no more titles to highlight.

    Fans have also pointed out that Star Wars has marketed the Jedi games a lot more as of late, which is very likely setting up for Jedi 3’s reveal.

    While it could just be Monaghan summing up, it feels to me more like he wants to say another game in that lineup that he simply can’t yet. Of course, he’s already noted some time ago after Survivor’s release that he’d be returning to the series, so it’s not like it’s some big surprise that he’s forbidden from mentioning, but it is still noticeable.

The incident, which took place on November 11th, is currently being investigated and police have reportedly taken a suspect into custody.

    "Officers got there [on November 11th]," Tustin police sergeant Christopher Peterson said in statement to Aftermath. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why.".

    "We’re relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," a spokesperson for InXile stated in a separate statement. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate.".

    It has been revealed that inXile are set to release steampunk RPG Clockwork Revolution next year. The studio, developers of the likes of Wasteland 3 and The Bard's Tale IV, are one of the few Xbox-owned studios not to have been affected - at least as of writing - by Microsoft's ongoing mass layoffs this year.

    In a recent development, since being declared in 2023, Clockwork Revolution's dripped with Bioshock-ish vibes and popped up semi-regularly at Xbox showcases. "Wield the power of an incredible device to travel back in time, changing the past and rewriting the future of the city you call home: the vibrant steampunk metropolis of Avalon," reads its Steam synopsis. "In this immersive RPG, you'll step into the shoes of Morgan Vanette, a fully customizable player-character and member of the Rotten Row Hooligans. Travel between past and present as you battle the ruthless Lady Ironwood, who has been manipulating time to keep the working class struggling while amassing immense wealth and power.".

    Best wishes to the staff at InXile, here's hoping that going forwards they're able to get with making what's looking to be an intriguingly funky game without enduring any more concerning incidents like this one.

    It has been revealed that one of the biggest reveals out of today’s Xbox Partner Preview showcase has been the fresh Stalker 2 expansion. The developer did tease some sort of announcement ahead of the event, but I don’t think an expansion was on many of our bingo cards.

    Sources indicate that cost of Hope is the substantial news; a new add-on that the developer has wisely decided to reveal fairly close to release. Or, at least, the planned release target.

    First off, Cost of Hope is set for release this summer. It’ll arrive on all current platforms simultaneously, meaning PC, Xbox, and PlayStation. The expansion is described as “non-linear”, and it takes place in the heartlands, deeper into the Zone.

    The story revolves around a conflict between Duty, and Freedom, two factions whose idea of the what the Zone is and their understanding of its possibilities differ widely. You’ll be playing as protagonist Skif once again, and the expansion’s events will run parallel to the main game.

    Industry observers note that GSC Game World indicates Cost of Hope will introduce two upcoming regions, offering dozens of hours of gameplay. We’ll get to actually explore the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant as part of the expansion, alongside the Iron Forest.

    Each of the two new regions will have its own hub area, NPCs, quests, activities and stories. Of course, it wouldn’t be a Stalker expansion without some new weapons, and Cost of Hope promises a few - some can even be seen in the trailer.

    The developer also confirmed that there’s one other story DLC in the works. Together with Heart of Chornobyl, and Cost of Hope all three will form a trilogy of interconnected stories. More details on Cost of Hope - including a release date - will be revealed sometime in the summer.

    "Flood of newly introduced AI games" kills retro homebrew competition

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that creating homebrew games for old consoles and computers is one of retro gaming's proudest traditions, and the Atari Homebrew Awards had been celebrating incredible community creations for the better part of a decade.
    • In a recent development, "Keeping up with the large number of AI assisted game development had become increasingly difficult as this year wore on with some developers even releasing multiple games a week with the aid of AI," host James, also known as ZeroPage Homebrew, says on the Atari Age forums (thanks, Time Extension).
    • James was "not at all interested in giving awards to the output of large language models, only to humans who coded their own games, but I quickly discovered that this was going to be more difficult than I thought.".
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that creating homebrew games for old consoles and computers is one of retro gaming's proudest traditions, and the Atari Homebrew Awards had been celebrating incredible community creations for the better part of a decade. But now, a wave of games built with AI has killed the ninth annual iteration of the competition as its host tries to figure out what to do.

    In a recent development, "Keeping up with the large number of AI assisted game development had become increasingly difficult as this year wore on with some developers even releasing multiple games a week with the aid of AI," host James, also known as ZeroPage Homebrew, says on the Atari Age forums (thanks, Time Extension). "This flood of new AI games forced me reevaluate the way games were qualified and judged for the upcoming AHAs.".

    James was "not at all interested in giving awards to the output of large language models, only to humans who coded their own games, but I quickly discovered that this was going to be more difficult than I thought.".

    You can probably guess at some of the issues James ran into. He didn't want to allow fully AI-generated games into the competition, but settling on a particular cutoff proved to be impossible. "There is no standard of reporting or calculating how much AI was used in each game," James notes, and even if there were a way to track it all, you'd have to make judgement calls. Is a little AI-generated code okay? Is using AI for testing alright?

    "We were always able to come up with a solution for small issues in previous years but the advent of AI marked a seismic shift in the way retro games were being made," James says. "I saw no path forward and made the difficult decision to suspend the Atari Homebrew Awards this year. This is an extremely upsetting conclusion for this event because honouring all the hard work the community put into these games is always a highlight of my year. I know many others feel the same way and I hope to be able to continue this tradition in the coming years as things settle into a upcoming normal.".

    In a recent development, the beauty of retro development scenes for many years is that they were labors of love. Developers were bringing Zelda games to PC and programming all-latest Atari 2600 games for little reason other than that they could. But AI code generation has made creating these projects dramatically easier, and fundamentally shifted the vibe of the community, as programmers with minimal skill build buggy, heartless games through Claude prompts. We still haven't figured out what the "new normal" is going to look like.

    These are the best retro consoles available today.

    Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

He's been covering games (with occasional dalliances in the worlds of anime and pro wrestling) since 2015, first as a freelancer, then as a news writer at PCGamesN for nearly five years. His love for games was sparked somewhere between Metal Gear Solid 2 and Knights of the Old Republic, and these days you can usually find him splitting his entertainment time between retro gaming, the latest major action-adventure title, or a long haul in American Truck Simulator.

    Today’s Genshin Impact Special Program has wrapped up, and it’s brought us some big news about the next major upgrade. Luna 6 is the next phase in the action RPG’s story, titled Song of the Welkin Moon: Rondo - Augured Homecoming.

    It’s set to arrive on April 8, bringing with it a tonne of upcoming content, including a substantial expansion to the original region of Mondstadt.

    As part of this upcoming enhancement, Mondstadt’s northern parts expand with new areas. The new Dornman Port is one thing, but the most exciting is the Temple of Space. This floating structure is home to Asmoday fragments, and is made up of different realms inspired by Liyue, Sumeru, and various other civilizations from around Teyvat. Launching with the update is a new mechanic that lets you manipulate the space to reveal hidden paths containing secrets.

    If you take the time to explore, you’ll find a lot to there to learn about Asmoday, Ruler of Space. There’s a latest boss to take on in the temple, too: Watcher: Fallen Vigil.

    Industry observers note that the only new character in Luna 6 is Linnea, who continues the current trend within HoYoverse games of focussing heavily on cute pink-haired animal-themed girls. Linnea is a 5-Star Geo Bow user who can really work with parties made up of Lunar-Crystallize characters, with her major gimmick being the ability to turn Hydro-Crystallize reactions into Lunar-Crystallize reactions.

    Linnea has a companion, Lumi, who allows her to increase the Lunar-Crystallize damage she deals, while also lowering her enemies’ Geo resistance. Linnea can also deliver either off-field Geo damage or a Lunar-Crystallize reaction hit with her Elemental Skill.

    According to recent reports, beyond that, she can heal the party using her Elemental Burst. If you take Linnea with you as you explore, she can help you discover rare animals, thanks to her innate naturalist abilities.

    This patch will also see Chasca get her first-ever rerun, and you’ll be able to roll for her in the first phase of Event Wishes. The second phase will feature no new characters and instead focus on Nefer and Lauma. There’s going to be another Chronicled Wish banner, this time specifically for Fontaine characters.

    You can look forward to a few other new arrivals in Luna 6, including The Nod-Krai Trade Expo, some quality of life updates to Miliastra Wonderland to up the number of players in each lobby, not to mention various other UI changes.

    Catch up on the latest Genshin Impact codes before you jump for some freebies.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

    10 Games to Play While Waiting for GTA VI to Go on Sale

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1509 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • After 13 years, Rockstar’s long awaited follow-up to Grand Theft Auto V, Grand Theft Auto VI, has finally arrived on Xbox and PlayStation consoles to widespread critical and financial acclaim, becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.
    • While millions of people are playing through GTA VI today, many are also holding off from playing the game until it goes on sale due its high price ranging from $80-$100 and massive file size of 212 GB, taking up a massive chunk of the base PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S internal storage.
    • For those gamers who are holding off on purchasing GTA VI until it goes on sale, here’s a list of 10 GTA VI-like titles they should check out in the meantime that are at the moment being sold at more affordable prices and balanced file sizes.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    After 13 years, Rockstar’s long awaited follow-up to Grand Theft Auto V, Grand Theft Auto VI, has finally arrived on Xbox and PlayStation consoles to widespread critical and financial acclaim, becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.

    While millions of people are playing through GTA VI today, many are also holding off from playing the game until it goes on sale due its high price ranging from $80-$100 and massive file size of 212 GB, taking up a massive chunk of the base PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S internal storage.

    For those gamers who are holding off on purchasing GTA VI until it goes on sale, here’s a list of 10 GTA VI-like titles they should check out in the meantime that are at the moment being sold at more affordable prices and balanced file sizes.

    Some people just enjoy Grand Theft Auto games for their comedy and freedom to sow chaos throughout cities and for people who enjoy that type of experience they should check out the FPS High on Life from the creators of Rick and Morty.

    Here, people play as a human as they wind up being teleported to the alien metropolis of Blim City to become an intergalactic bounty hunter with living guns called Gatlians guiding them to take down the G3 Cartel that intends on turning the entire human race into drugs.

    High on Life is as ridiculous and hilarious as it sounds, essentially being a perfect translation of Rick and Morty’s signature comedy style to video game form, and it will certainly give players many laughs as they wait for GTA VI to go on sale.

    Ever since Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, flying all kinds of aircraft has been an integral part of the GTA experience and for those who enjoy flying more than driving in the franchise, there’s no better game to check out while waiting for GTA VI sales than Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024.

    The latest entry in the long-running Microsoft Flight Simulator series, Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is the most advanced publicly available flight simulator, allowing players to learn how to fly a wide variety of aircraft in first or third-person such as airships, gliders, hot air balloons, jets, and more.

    Not only that, but the game additionally allows players to fly any aircraft across the planet’s most famous natural and urban environments such as Zion National Park, Mount Fuji, London, and Miami which is what GTA VI’s Vice City is directly based on.

    Even more so than flying, driving has arguably been the defining factor of the GTA franchise with the series initially starting out as a top-down driving-focused game and if GTA fans wanted to check out the most advanced realistic racing game, then they’d have to play Forza Horizon 6.

    Currently an Xbox Series X|S console exclusive, Forza Horizon 6 has players journey to the rural and urban streets of a stylised version of Tokyo as they strive to qualify for the Horizon Festival or simply drive around Japan’s wondrous landscapes using over 500 cars.

    There’s far more to do in Forza Horizon 6 than just driving around Japan as players can customize a massive estate filled with garages and custom tracks or players can customize public roads to use in multiplayer races.

    Some people may enjoy the GTA series for the driving, flying, or comedy but oftentimes people like those games for the freedom to cause chaos in any way they desire, with one game that offers a similar style of player freedom being Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster.

    An RE Engine remake of 2006’s Dead Rising, Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster follows the photojournalist Frank West as he sneaks his way into a Willamette, Colorado mall to cover a zombie outbreak only to get trapped in the mall and attempt to investigate the outbreak’s origins.

    While players can stick to completing the game’s many time limited narrative cases, players can instantly go about slaying zombies and psychopaths in any way they want by using practically anything found in the mall such as jugs of orange juice, CDs, katanas, potted plants, shopping carts, and more.

    If people want to experience a game with a similar story and setting to GTA VI, there are actually a few good games to choose from with one of the more underrated options being Hangar 13’s Mafia III.

    The first Mafia game to not be developed by series creator Illusion Softworks, Mafia III follows Vietnam War veteran turned crime lord Lincoln Clay in the U.S. gulf coast city of Fresh Bordeaux as he sets out to avenge his adoptive father and brother after they were killed by the Marcano crime family.

    While Mafia III isn’t set in the present day, it still features a similarly enthralling and emotional story, one that tackles social concerns of late 1960s America and features multiple different endings depending on Clay’s actions and choices during his campaign to take down the local mafia.

    When it comes to video games centered around crime, most people wouldn’t consider an entry from the war-focused Battlefield series to be one but in 2015, Visceral Games did just that by creating the crime and police centered Battlefield Hardline.

    Visceral’s final game ever released, Battlefield Hardline’s campaign follows Miami Police Detective Nick Mendoza attempting to take down drug dealers and suppliers in the Florida based city only to discover corruption in the MPD and wind up being framed for a crime he didn’t commit.

    Hardline may not have been the game traditional Battlefield fans wanted at the time of its release but Visceral’s writing and gameplay prowess managed to make it stand as not only one of the most unique Battlefield games but also one of the most intriguing and cinematic.

    Ubisoft is famous for creating immersive open-world titles like the numerous entries from the Assassin’s Creed and Far Cry series but it wasn’t until 2014 that the publisher decided to make a more grounded GTA-like experience with Watch Dogs.

    Set in Chicago and the same universe as the Assassin’s Creed franchise, Watch Dogs follows hacker Aiden Pearce who, after a heist goes wrong, sets out to find the people responsible for putting a hit on him resulting in the death of his niece Lena.

    What ensues is an action-packed yet stealthy gaming experience as Pearce is able to hack particularly every piece of technology in the city from cellphones to trains and construction equipment to aid him in tracking his enemies down in between instances where Pearce has to steal cars or engage in gun fights.

    While Mafia III and Watch Dogs are fun GTA-like titles, neither of them compare to the pure chaos and drama that can be unleashed in CD Projekt Red’s ambitious first-person, open-world, action RPG Cyberpunk 2077.

    The latest brand-new game developed by the makers of The Witcher game series, Cyberpunk 2077 has players embody the cyborg mercenary V in the futuristic and crime-filled metropolis of Night City as they get caught up in a movement to take down the corrupt Arasaka Corporation.

    Cyberpunk 2077’s reputation may have been marred by a buggy 2020 launch but it has since gone on to become one of the best modern RPGs thanks to beneficial updates and its Phantom Liberty DLC making the game’s core combat, dialogue, and side activities all the more fun.

    GTA VI is set in the present day but its greatest gaming influence on a technical and narrative level is undoubtedly Rockstar Games’ previous modern gaming big hit, Red Dead Redemption 2.

    Set roughly 12 years before Red Dead Redemption 1 at the turn of the 20th century, Red Dead Redemption 2 primarily follows Van der Linde gang member Arthur Morgan as he and the rest of the gang struggle to survive against rival gangs, nature itself, and the ever-dominating presence of industrialized civilization.

    Before GTA VI, Red Dead Redemption 2 was Rockstar’s most cinematic and immersive game ever made as not only did it feature a far more serious and emotional story than any GTA game before but it allowed players to do all kinds of things in the old west such as hunting wildlife, taking care of horses, crafting materials, and more.

    For anybody still waiting on GTA VI or consoles with large internal storage capacities to go on sale, the number one game they have to play in the meantime is the multi console generational juggernaut itself, GTA V.

    GTA VI is making records now but GTA V was a phenomenon all on its own for over a decade as it constantly outsold almost every other game on the market for years on end partly due to its campaign following Franklin, Michael, and Trevor in Los Santos but mainly due to its ever evolving GTA Online.

    With GTA VI’s iteration of GTA Online likely months away from launch, it’ll be good to finish up whatever players haven’t done yet in GTA Online, such as its many heists and mode customization options, before everyone migrates over to GTA VI’s multiplayer.

    We were all expecting Grand Theft Auto 6 to have a lot of easter eggs, secrets, and discoveries for players across the wide world of Leonida, but there's even more than any of us could have imagined.

    The community has been finding all of these wild secrets over the past few weeks, but one of the most surprising comes in the form of a layered nod to Nintendo's flagship series. Here's how to see it.

    Sources indicate that to reach one of GTA 6's most surprising easter eggs, you'll need to head to the bottom part of Moreau in Lummox County, to the north of the overall map. The location you're looking for is a dilapidated building, which we've marked on the map above since it can be quite difficult to make out until you know what you're looking for.

    In a recent development, once here, you'll need to smoke the bong that you'll find on a table in the middle of the building, next to a yellow box you can open for some cash. Beyond being a reference to all of those obvious jokes about Mario and mushrooms, doing so will cause a nearly invisible block to show up at the top of the ruined building. You'll then need to climb up and shoot the block, which will cause it to drop two hats.

    It has been revealed that these hats, a purple one with J on the front and a teal one with L on the front, are an obvious but delightful reference to Super Mario. You don't need both characters there to get both hats, as you can pick them up as either protagonist. Just be careful they don't go flying too far and get lost.

    Recent findings suggest that as I found out the hard way, you really don't want both characters there while you're trying to climb the building, as they'll consistently knock each other off. It does make for a funny sight, though.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A hacker has pleaded guilty to a number of online crimes, including the 2022 breach of Rockstar Games which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net.
    • The BBC report that, on November 16th, Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17.
    • Kurtaj carried out the 2022 Rockstar hack while on bail for other hacking offences and being housed at a Travelodge hotel under police protection, the latter on account of rival hackers threatening to attack him over stolen Bitcoin stashes.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A hacker has pleaded guilty to a number of online crimes, including the 2022 breach of Rockstar Games which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net.

    The BBC report that, on November 16th, Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Kurtaj, now aged 21, was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial. He'll be sentenced at a later date.

    Kurtaj carried out the 2022 Rockstar hack while on bail for other hacking offences and being housed at a Travelodge hotel under police protection, the latter on account of rival hackers threatening to attack him over stolen Bitcoin stashes. The Rockstar hack was reportedly done using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into the hotel room's TV, plus a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

    90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by that hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the manufacturer contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

    Earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by "Cyberleek" posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent organization Take-Two quickly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

    Recent findings suggest that hopefully with the game's console release later this week, those will be the only two GTA 6 leaks which have to be added to the annals of gaming history. As much as marketing can leave a bad taste in the mouth, especially when it barely reveals anything of the actual product being advertised, neither of the GTA 6 leaks served much of a purpose beyond forcing people to waste some time and energy talking about the perpetrators.

There's a viral video going around showcasing an incredibly elaborate Easter egg that I'm convinced would've remained a secret for a long, long while if it weren't for someone with an encyclopedic knowledge of GTA: Vice City and its many cheat codes.

    That person is a content creator who goes by Memeio, who says they are "the first person to ever crack this code in the world," and I believe them. But before we get into it, here's your spoiler warning in case you want to try finding this one on your own at some point, although that seems unlikely.

It's a hell of a mind trip to see, and I can only imagine it would be even more surreal to experience in the game.

    As Memeio explains in the below video, the actual process of unlocking this Easter egg involves pressing various buttons and pulling various levers in a precise order at different substations across the map, but finding out the right order of everything took "literally 3 days of rotting and searching for power stations.".

    Recent findings suggest that I discovered this GTA 6 easter egg about 3 days ago, here it is in video form, I think I'm the first person to ever crack this code in the world so enjoy! #GTA6 https://t.co/vTORjUlYNiNovember 23, 2026.

    In a recent development, memeio was first clued in by an extremely subtle auditory cue that Memeio claims is "a sound effect from Vice City," which apparently plays when you power up the radio tower in Key Lento. From there, individual letters appearing on the exteriors of substations spelled out a phrase from GTA: Vice City that correlates with a cheat code, which Memeio translated to an order by which to press the levers at all 12 substations. How they came up with this, no one knows, but it is really frikkin' cool.

    In a recent development, seeing stuff like this makes me wonder what bigger, even more complicated easter eggs might be hiding in GTA, and then I get kind of sad because I know I'll never have the patience to find them on my own. Cheers to people like Memeio.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales.
    • All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they declared a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".
    • Sources indicate that the lawyers in question are from Robbins LLP, who specialise in "shareholder, whistleblower, antitrust, & consumer litigation".
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales. The class action lawsuit in question claims that Intel's distribution and manufacturing partners have had to deal with "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", and that the gains from Intel's investments in AI datacenters aren't enough to make up for slowing sales of PCs to regular Josephines who just want fancy boxes they can play Deadlock on.

    All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they declared a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".

    Sources indicate that the lawyers in question are from Robbins LLP, who specialise in "shareholder, whistleblower, antitrust, & consumer litigation". In a press release, they say they've filed suit on behalf of anybody who bought Intel stock from July 23rd to October 29th this year.

    The suit claims that Intel neglected to tell investors that falling PC and component sales were having a "materially greater negative impact" on their third financial quarter 2026 Client Computing and Physical AI Groupresults than Intel had previously stated – to the tune of "hundreds of millions of dollars" in revenue shrinkage, compared to the previous quarter, with the situation still expected to "worsen".

    They also accuse the manufacturer of keeping schtum about the aforesaid "massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", together with the fact that "any positive impacts to Intel’s business and financial results resulting from data center construction and other aspects of the AI boom were more than offset by the negative effects on the Company’s business and financial results resulting from the PC market slowdown and the excess inventory buildup described above.".

    Finally, they say Intel bosses have failed to disclose that they're struggling to procure an adequate supply of substrates – that is, materials used to create the base layer of chips, circuit boards and similar components. As such, the lawyers claim, Intel couldn't "ramp up production to meet data center CPU demand even if the Organization chose to divert production resources because of a slowdown in PC-related sales.".

    It has been revealed that once the Godzilla of personal computing, Intel haven't been having a brilliant few years. Back in 2024, they recorded a multi-billion dollar quarterly loss, pushing then-CEO Pat Gelsinger to resign. As regards sales of gaming PCs, they've fallen behind AMD, though they've reportedly taken some ground back recently as regards desktop CPUs. As regards graphics cards, they have long been dwarfed by Nvidia.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    I'm convinced that Lucia is a clone in Grand Theft Auto 6 — at least, in my playthrough. If you happen on a little side quest called The Final Flush, where you help a conspiracy theorist uncover the secret machinations of Big Sewage, things get a little weird. Weird enough that yes, I really am convinced Lucia is a clone. Just don't let the FIB hear me posting about that on Snapmatic, yeah?

    In all seriousness, this is one of those oddities in GTA 6 where you don't really understand what's happening, things veer a little X-Files, and then you're handed a permanent stamina upgrade for your troubles as though you haven't been wading through literal crap.

    Sources indicate that like all good encounters, you start The Final Flush by scanning a QR code on a handwritten poster by a toilet that screams "STOP! DON'T FLUSH." I also found the same poster in the storage compartment of a pawn shop, but if you want a reliable way to begin the mission instead of going on a Vice City crime spree until you happen across one, head to the north of Corsair Key in Mariana County and enter the only building on the entire island - the toilet.

    Use the WaiNK IT app to scan the QR code (#NOFLUSHERS) and you'll get a message asking you to reply "TRUTH" to join the movement. If you decide to embrace your inner tinfoil hat, you'll get a follow-up message telling you to meet the sender at Frank's Waffles in Vice City, whereupon arriving you'll need to repeat the code: 00-00-02.

    Drive to Frank's Waffles, and you'll see an older man muttering to himself at a booth by the toilets. This is the colorful Dr. Merle, a conspiracy theorist with an ingenious blueprint: swallow a tracker, poop it out, and follow it to the source.

    Of course, as Lucia rightfully points out (you can also do this mission with Jason), he could've just thrown the tracker in the toilet and saved himself the trouble. But he waffles about how Node is too smart for that, and that he needs to be stealthier.

    If you return to Frank's Waffles and check the toilet later, well, I decided not to include the screenshot.

    Sources indicate that the point is, supposedly, Big Sewage is harvesting Leonidan DNA through their poop to make clones of its citizens, and Dr. Merle wants to get to the bottom of it.

    Immediately after depositing the tracker, Dr. Merle will ask you to drive his van as he yells directions at you. You can take a guess at where the tracker in the sewage pipes leads — the sewage plant.

    Just make sure you have the compass enabled, as you won't get a trail on your mini-map to follow, only sporadic directions from Dr. Merle as he tells you to drive east, north, and in whatever direction the pipes are leading.

    In a recent development, eventually, you will get close enough that a waypoint appears on the beach. Park the van on the coast and follow Dr. Merle on foot along the fence, where he'll start lockpicking a gate to get you inside.

    Recent findings suggest that dr. Merle will ask you to keep watch while he very slowly works a lock that Lucia and Jason could pick in seconds. You can't really do much though, because it's a chain-link fence that security can easily see through.

    So, when a van pulls up asking what exactly you're doing, select 'Defuse' to tell the worker you're fixing the gate. They won't believe you, but it will buy you enough time to get inside and start sneaking about.

    Industry observers note that once inside, head to the pink area marked on your map. You can either talk to the workers and lie that you're electricians, or sneak past them through the double doors into the adjacent building (like with all interiors, it's marked by a darker shade of blue).

    In a recent development, here, Dr. Merle will break down and ramble about how close he got to finding out the truth, only to be thwarted by concrete, as the tracker is right below your feet. This is where things take a turn. His poop-laden tracker isn't just lurking in underground pipes, there's a secret facility.

    According to recent reports, head to the balcony overseeing the room where there's a control panel with three buttons. Turn all the lights on the panel green (press the bottom two) and then interact with the main lever. Right where Dr. Merle is sitting, a secret staircase will be revealed leading to a strange chamber.

    Naturally, like with any conspiracy theorist worth his salt, Dr. Merle puts his idea to the test and climbs into the chamber. It swiftly fills with a strange, viscous green liquid, and he asks you — Jason or Lucia — to press the button on the control panel and quite literally flush him. Do it.

    Recent findings suggest that the room blares with the sound of the agitated water authority warning you that the police are en route and that the chamber is toxic and should not be entered. But if you want a permanent stamina upgrade, I'm afraid you have to get inside and follow Dr. Merle's example.

    You'll enter first-person while it fills with that strange green liquid again, and bizarrely, you wake up outside your safehouse, unclear how you got there, stamina upgrade in hand.

    According to recent reports, okay, I'm not only convinced that my Lucia is a clone. I have proof. And this is where the guide takes a turn. After completing The Significant Flush, you can find a disturbing little easter egg revealing what exactly happened in the chamber.

    According to recent reports, head north to Lummox County and travel to the eastern island. Make sure you don't stumble onto Hyde Island, or you'll end up being hunted for sport.

    Near the tip, there's a sealed bunker. Enter the code '3612' to open the door, and head on inside. There's no reward here, just a disturbing revelation that will change how you see the rest of the game.

    Recent findings suggest that through the bunker and down a ladder, you'll see three corpses — so long as you've done the mission first: Dr. Merle, whoever you put in the chamber, and an unknown bald man (I checked his face, it isn't Jason).

    Naturally, as you can see in the video embedded above, I brought Jason along so he could find out that the Lucia at home is really a clone, which makes every single text and interaction feel just a little bit off. But hey, a free stamina upgrade is a free stamina upgrade.

    Or... maybe these are discarded clones. Who's to say?

    GTA 6: How to Find the Secret Satan Boss

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (676 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • GTA 6 has a ton of secrets to find throughout the large map of Leonida.
    • One of the coolest easter eggs in the game is the secret Satan boss fight.
    • According to recent reports, if you are looking to take down Satan himself, this guide explains everything you need to know.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    GTA 6 has a ton of secrets to find throughout the large map of Leonida. Some examples include the Kraken deep underwater, UFOs, and even a Mario and Luigi reference.

    One of the coolest easter eggs in the game is the secret Satan boss fight. Not only is it a really trippy mission, but it also rewards the player with one of the best weapons in the game.

    According to recent reports, if you are looking to take down Satan himself, this guide explains everything you need to know. Here’s how to find the secret Satan boss fight in GTA 6.

    In a recent development, to find the secret Satan boss in GTA 6, you must travel to the northern side of Port Gellhorn and visit the house with “Welcome to the Hellhole!” written on it. You can find the exact location of this house in the image of Port Gellhorn below.

    When you arrive at this house, the garage will either be open or closed. The Satan boss fight event can only be triggered if the garage is open, so if it happens to be shut when you arrive, then you’ll have to come back another time. This event all comes down to RNG, but there are ways to increase your chances.

    According to recent reports, first, the garage has a higher chance of being open late at night. For example, it was open for me around 10:00 PM, so I recommend only visiting the Hellhole house around this time.

    Keep in mind that the event won’t trigger if you just wait outside the house. Instead, I recommend using the RydeMe app to fast travel to another location and back to the house multiple times until the garage opens. This worked for me after five attempts.

    Recent findings suggest that once the garage finally opens, walk inside to find two men having some drinks. They will ask you if you want a beer, which you should grab from the cooler next to the couch.

    Recent findings suggest that for the next couple of minutes, make sure you don’t do anything to piss these guys off. You can talk to them, but don’t choose the “provoke” dialogue option or throw a bottle to mess up the event. Instead, wait patiently until their van arrives.

    Recent findings suggest that when the van arrives, the men will ask you to join them for their upcoming ritual. You should agree here and climb into the back of the van, which will then transport you to another location with a bonfire.

    Next, get out of the van and make your way to the bonfire to celebrate with the two Satanists, and wait until they tell you to look into the fire. Once the prompt “look into the fire” pops up, hold down the button to do just that.

    Looking into the fire will teleport you to hell, where you’ll have to fight a wave of Satan’s demons and Satan himself.

    Satan is not very difficult to defeat, but the fight can be a bit confusing. What you want to do here is shoot the exploding enemies that are running toward you, which will turn Satan’s health bar red.

    According to recent reports, once the health bar is red, you want to shoot at Satan to drain his health. When the health bar turns back to black, you want to repeat the process and kill the surrounding enemies to turn the bar red again.

    Doing this a few times will have Satan going down fairly rapidly. Once you kill Satan, you will teleport back to the real world.

    When players respawn back to the real world after fighting Satan in GTA 6, they will be granted a permanent health increase. Additionally, they’ll be able to claim the Hellspawn Cumshot 12 Shotgun next to the large throne.

    This shotgun is extremely powerful and is one of the best guns I have found in the game so far, so I recommend equipping it for any upcoming missions you have.

    Latest Update: Each latest GTA moves the series closer and closer to the original Mafia, the open-world game that bettered Rockstar

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (934 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • This week sees the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, the open-world crime 'em up that's been in development for at least eight years and has been waited on by fans for even longer.
    • Released less than a year after Grand Theft Auto 3, Mafia is perhaps a more prescient example of Rockstar's future than their own.
    • Set in Lost Heaven, a shoe-in for 1930s Chicago, Illinois, you play through Tommy Angelo's rise from a taxi driver, who has a chance run in with the Salieri crime family, to one of the gang's main enforcers in their fight against their rivals, the Morellos.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    This week sees the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, the open-world crime 'em up that's been in development for at least eight years and has been waited on by fans for even longer. Naturally, over on PC we're still waiting for a port to be unveiled, let alone a release date to circle in our calendars. But, as happens whenever a latest GTA is on the horizon, I think about Mafia: City of Lost Heaven.

    Released less than a year after Grand Theft Auto 3, Mafia is perhaps a more prescient example of Rockstar's future than their own.

    Set in Lost Heaven, a shoe-in for 1930s Chicago, Illinois, you play through Tommy Angelo's rise from a taxi driver, who has a chance run in with the Salieri crime family, to one of the gang's main enforcers in their fight against their rivals, the Morellos.

    In a recent development, the influences on developers Illusion Softworks are obviously cinematic, with whole sequences ripped from The Godfather films and Goodfellas (and I'd argue there's a sprinkling of Once Upon A Time In America for good measure). A habit they share with Rockstar, who also pull liberally from crime films that share the settings of their games. But Illusion Softworks are also clearly interested in capturing the history of the Prohibition era, too. The story begins in the aftermath of the 1929 Wall Street Crash and the depression that followed, running through until the late 30s, and you see that time pass in the city around you. Buildings that are under construction at the start of the game are completed by its end, a used car lot in Chinatown sits empty for most of the game until business picks up with the economy, but most enjoyable of all is that the cars driving the streets change. At first the roads are filled with Ford Model-T-inspired vehicles that basically look like horse carriages with engines, but by the end of the game they've all become much sleeker creatures that have left their early carriage influences behind.

    It has been revealed that the city Illusion Softworks built also has a dedication to verisimilitude that we see Rockstar adopting in their later games. As you drive Lost Heaven's streets, you must pay attention to speed limits and red lights, as speeding and running traffic lights will both earn you a fine if a policeman spots you. For fans of public transport, there are streetcars and overhead trams you can ride to navigate the city, too. Two other touches I love: when you reload your gun, you dump the whole clip instead of returning the unfired bullets to a magic ammo reservoir, and vehicles can run out of fuel if you drive them too far.

    In a recent development, much had been made of all the simulations running under the surface of Grand Theft Auto 6, such as fully realised cloud formation, a smell reaction system, and… fuel tanks that can run empty. No doubt they're significantly more impressive than what's on show in Mafia, and this isn't about putting the two games against each other (even if one of them was likely made for less than the other studio spent on coffee runs across its eight-year development). Nor is it about saying history recognised the wrong game: Grand Theft Auto 3 was a huge step forward in open-world gaming and Mafia was recognised and celebrated in its time. It's about something else.

    Industry observers note that back in 2002, Illusion Softworks offered a different kind of open-world crime game. One that was more mature despite having a lower age rating. Grand Theft Auto was undoubtedly more influential, sparking imitators that mostly opted to follow its tone and sensibilities – Saints Row began in a similar place to GTA 3 and as the series continued leaned further into the silliness and parody, for instance. But while for many years Mafia stood as a sign to an open world path that could have been taken, the longer Grand Theft Auto series has gone on, the more Rockstar have found their way toward the example set by Illusion Softworks. The games are still aiming for bombastic comedy at times, but they're also interested in the likes of newly-arrived-in-America Niko Belic, or Michael de Santa, a retired criminal haunted by his past. They're much richer protagonists than Claude, the silent character you play in GTA 3.

    Industry observers note that the Mafia series has continued, marked by ideas that remain as interesting as what was on show in the original. In Mafia 3, you play Lincoln Clay, a black soldier returned from the war in Vietnam and brought into the family. Set in a take on Newly introduced Orleans, Louisiana, during the civil rights movement, you face overt racism. Linger too long in white, wealthy neighbourhoods and the residents will call on the police to move you along. And the Definitive Edition remake of the first game, released in 2020, is a rare example of a game that both captures the spirit of the original and justifies its existence by expanding and bettering the story. Though I don't think any of its sequels have been as innovative, nor as forward thinking, as the first game.

    I don't want to come across as Rockstar-bashing. The studio have continued to push the open-world genre forward with every release and I want to see what other developers lift from GTA 6 for their own games. But I'm even more pleased that as the studio's aged, their work has grown closer to Illusion Softworks'.

Following reports from earlier in 2026 that development had already started on the upcoming episodes ahead of season 3's release, Amazon Studios confirmed that pre-production has begun. The third season's finale sets up plenty more to come in the Lord of the Rings prequel as well.

If that wasn't enough to tide you over until we see more, check out our guide to watching The Lord of the Rings in order too for the ultimate rewatch.

    We'll be getting into spoilers for The Rings of Power season 3 below, so make sure you're up to date.

    The Rings of Power season 4 has been confirmed by Prime Video. Ahead of the release of the show's finale on November 24, Amazon Studios confirmed that pre-production was underway at Shepperton Studios, where the series is filmed.

    It's clear that Amazon Studios has been working to give themselves as much of a head start as possible to allow for smaller gaps between seasons.

    It has been revealed that when it was confirmed that development was kicking off, The Hollywood Reporter suggested filming could begin in early 2027. Based on season 3, we can get an idea about what this might mean for a potential release date.

    Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

    Season 3 started filming in May 2025 before it was released in November 2026. Based on a similar schedule, if filming starts in early 2027, we could see The Rings of Power season 4 in mid-to-late 2028.

    We'll keep you in the loop with any updates on the next season when we get them.

    The Rings of Power season 3 saw Sauron reach the height of his powers after forging the One Ring. In episode 7, he was finally able to create the weapon that would allow him to control all of the other rings. In the season finale, he prepped for his final battle with the help of Pallando and the peoples of Rhûn.

    Recent findings suggest that however, before he could reach the battlefield, Gandalf was able to bring Pallando back to the light, even if he was killed in the process. The light of his return casts off Sauron's power over the people of Rhûn, who abandon the fight. Faced with just his army of Orcs against the men of Númenor and the Elves, it's not looking so promising for Sauron.

    According to recent reports, he decides to give himself up, walking over to Ar-Pharazôn and kneeling before him, allowing him to be taken prisoner by Númenor. However, we wouldn't be so sure this is the Dark Lord giving in. This is Sauron, after all, and he will definitely have a nefarious plan.

    No plot details have been revealed yet, but it seems like this is where the show will pick up again. We're also likely going to get more time jumps going forward. Speaking to GamesRadar+, co-showrunner Patrick McKay mentioned this is their current initiative.

    He explained: "I think from the very beginning, we aspired the show to compress the time that's in the books, but also to have significant jumps forward in time for characters to age, for kingdoms to rise or fall, and I think you know there will probably be some jumps in the future.".

    Based on where we are right now in the Lord of the Rings timeline, there are several potential avenues that The Rings of Power season 4 may cover. The major moment in Middle-earth's history that looks likely to be explored is the fall of Númenor.

    This has been building for a while, but in Tolkien's work we know that Ar-Pharazôn captures Sauron and brings him to Númenor. This is what's implied at the end of The Rings of Power season 3.

    Here, Sauron is able to manipulate the king, influencing him to make war against the Valar. This sets off a chain of cataclysmic events that ends with Númenor buried under a huge wave.

    Sources indicate that not everyone dies, though, as Elendil and his sons Isildur and Anárion, alongside some of the other Faithful, escape the fall by traveling to Middle-earth. Here, they found Arnor and Gondor, two key locales in Lord of the Rings history.

    Sauron also loses his ability to take fair form after Númenor falls, with his spirit remaining in the One Ring. It's not yet clear whether the show will follow this or make some substantial changes in the coming season.

    The Rings of Power season 4 cast has not yet been confirmed but we can expect most of the lead roles to be back, aside from the casualties in the season finale (RIP Pallando).

    There is no Rings of Power season 4 trailer yet. We expect we'll be waiting quite a while before we see one too, given that cameras have yet to roll.

    In a recent development, with season 3, the trailer was released at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, just over three months before the show debuted. We expect season 4 will follow a similar timeframe.

    When Amazon Studios secured the rights from the Tolkien estate, they made the commitment to five seasons of the prequel show. The showrunners, J.D. Payne and Patrick McKay, have been very open that this remains their long-term proposal as well.

    Recent findings suggest that speaking to French publication Le Journal du Geek in late 2026, McKay reiterated this too. "We have a blueprint, we know it ends with five seasons. That's still the plan," he told them.

    Recent findings suggest that of course, plans can change, and the show may end at season 4, but we would be pretty surprised if it did. This means that we should be in for two more epic seasons to conclude this story.

    For more, check out our The Rings of Power season 3 review and The Rings of Power season 3 ending explained for a full breakdown.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nintendo's GameCube title Wave Race: Blue Storm has today made a splash on the Switch Online + Expansion Pack service.

    In a recent development, if you have an active subscription and access to a Switch 2, you can play it right now via the 'Nintendo Classics' GameCube app. Here's Nintendo's official description:.

    "Storm warning! Prepare to ride the waves! Take to the water in this watercraft-racing game, released for the Nintendo GameCube™ system in 2001. Compete in contests of speed and technique—either racing against your rivals or going up against your own records. As you race across the waves, you can see the skies changes from calm and sunny to surging storms... Weather conditions can affect visibility, water levels, and the height of the waves over the course of a race, so you'll need to be prepared for whatever comes!".

    This jet ski racer was a follow-up to Wave Race 64 (also available on the Nintendo Classics service) and arrived in 2001/02.

    It has been revealed that the game's water and weather effects were a stunning showcase on Nintendo's new hardware at the time, and the water physics in the title also raised the bar. Japan has received the same title on the Nintendo Classics service this week.

    Alongside this latest game upgrade (Version 2.2.0), you can now also turn off the "border graphic" when playing GameCube titles. However, the player icon remains on the screen.

    Please note voting will score the game in your games collection.

    In a recent development, will you be revisiting this title? Let us know in the comments.

    Heartopia celebrates 30 million downloads with new outfits, permanent price cuts

    📅 06 Apr 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (279 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Vg247

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that heartopia has kicked off a new event to celebrate passing 30 million downloads.
    • The event kicked off on Saturday, bringing some new themed content to the game.
    • Whimsical Tea Party’s biggest addition are the newly introduced outfits, including the Wandering Traveler, and the Duke Bunny outfits.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that heartopia has kicked off a new event to celebrate passing 30 million downloads. Just a couple of weeks after delivering the vintage Hollywood-themed Dreamlight Cinematics event, developer XD Games has revealed The Whimsical Tea Party, a limited-time Gilded Acorn Exhibition.

    The event kicked off on Saturday, bringing some new themed content to the game.

    Whimsical Tea Party’s biggest addition are the newly introduced outfits, including the Wandering Traveler, and the Duke Bunny outfits. Each outfit is available in three different colours. Another thing Heartopia events bring are building materials sets.

    Industry observers note that this one adds the Labyrinth furniture building materials set, the Hedgehog & Flamingo mallet, and the Cheshire Cat pet costume. Speaking of outfits, XD Games is dropping the in-game prices for a number of items permanently.

    Sources indicate that all original pet outfits now cost 66.7% less. Those of the Common variety will now cost 10 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, instead of the previous 30. Rare pet outfits will cost 5 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, down from 15.

    In a recent development, keeping with the theme of freebies, Heartopia is also celebrating surpassing 30 million downloads worldwide by giving all players a small gift package in-game. This freebie is available until May 29, so you should have enough time to claim it.

    For comprehensive guidance on where to find birds, bugs, and fish, check out our Heartopia bird locations, Heartopia bug locations, and Heartopia fish locations guides. If you’re instead looking to find some wild vegetables for those cooking recipes, hit those links. And, as ever, it doesn’t hurt to see if you missed out on any Heartopia codes.
